items.title: CLI exits successfully even when transforms report errors
items.recommendation: When `totalErrors > 0`, set `process.exitCode = 1` or throw after printing the summary, and avoid printing the success message. If partial writes are possible, make the summary explicitly say the run completed with errors.
items.reproduction: Run `anvil-codemod imports` on input that causes `rewriteImportsInFile` to return one or more errors. The CLI reports `Errors: N`, then prints `Changes applied successfully.` and exits with status 0.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this CLI feature, and the current files show no assertion of exit status or summary output when transform errors occur.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CLI test that stubs or fixtures `rewriteImportsInFile` to return an error, invokes `imports`, and asserts non-zero exit status plus no `Changes applied successfully` message.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the `imports` action error summary/exit handling in `tools/codemods/src/cli.ts` and add focused CLI coverage for transform-error behaviour.

items.title: Context test constructs diagnostics with stale field names
items.recommendation: Update the Kindling test helper to construct the canonical `Diagnostic` shape with `schema_version` and `summary`, then adjust any Kindling code that still reads legacy `schema` or `message` fields.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --dir packages/anvil-driver-client typecheck` in a configuration that includes `src/**/*.test.ts`; TypeScript should report excess `schema`/`message` properties and missing `schema_version`/`summary` on the `Diagnostic` return value.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The Kindling tests are present, but Vitest transpilation does not necessarily enforce TypeScript structural errors, and the helper's runtime fields can still be sufficient for the Kindling builder if it only reads severity/source/mode.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Keep the helper typed as `Diagnostic` after replacing `schema` with `schema_version` and `message` with `summary`; ensure package typecheck includes this test file or add a compile-time assertion fixture for `fromMidEditResponse` inputs.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/kindling/types.test.ts and, if needed, the Kindling response/input type definitions that consume diagnostics.

items.title: Admin secrets can be supplied in process arguments
items.recommendation: Do not accept admin API keys or raw tokens as command-line values. Keep `ANVIL_ADMIN_KEY` for the admin key, and use stdin, an interactive hidden prompt, a file descriptor, or a non-secret token identifier/hash for token revocation. If compatibility is required, deprecate these options and emit a warning before removal.
items.reproduction: Run a long enough admin operation as `anvil-admin --key secret revoke --token raw-token ...` and inspect the process command line from the same host while it is running; the secret values are part of argv.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise error handling and `--help` only; they do not assert how sensitive inputs are accepted or rejected.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add CLI parser tests that reject `--key <value>` and raw `--token <value>` once replaced, and cover the supported non-argv secret path such as env/stdin/prompt input.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/admin-cli/src/index.ts` option definitions and the corresponding config/command input plumbing for admin key and token revocation secret handling.

items.title: Shell integration tests source the wrapper path without shell quoting
items.recommendation: Add a small shell-quoting helper for paths embedded in `bash -c` scripts, or avoid string interpolation by passing the script path as an argument/environment variable and sourcing `"$ANVIL_RUN_SCRIPT"`. Apply it consistently at all three call sites.
items.reproduction: Run the crate tests from a checkout path containing a space, or adjust the test to source a copied `anvil-run.sh` from a temp directory named with a space; the generated `. /path/with space/anvil-run.sh` command will not source the intended file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests use the current `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, which usually has no whitespace or shell metacharacters, so the unquoted path bug is not exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Copy `shell/anvil-run.sh` into a temp directory whose name contains a space, source that copied path through the same test helper, and assert the dispatcher still invokes the stub.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `crates/anvil-run/tests/shell_integration.rs` to quote or otherwise safely pass `script_path()` in all generated bash snippets.

items.title: close can be overwritten by an in-flight connect
items.recommendation: Track a connection generation/abort token or an active connect promise. After transport.connect() resolves, verify the client is still in the expected generation and not closed before assigning transport/state; otherwise close the just-opened transport and leave state closed. Also make concurrent connect() calls share the same in-flight promise or reject/no-op while connecting.
items.reproduction: Use a transportFactory whose connect() returns a manually resolved promise. Call const connecting = client.connect(); await client.close(); then resolve the transport connect promise and await connecting. A subsequent client.request(...) is allowed because openTransport() changed state from closed back to connected.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests cover close() after a completed connect and idempotent close, but they do not cover close() while connect() or reconnect is still awaiting transport.connect().
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a DriverClient test with a manually controlled fake transport.connect() promise: start connect(), call close() before resolving it, resolve connect(), then assert connect either rejects/settles without resurrecting and request() still rejects with anvil-driver-closed; also assert the late transport is closed.
items.minimumFixScope: DriverClient lifecycle state around connect/openTransport/close.

items.title: local close of in-flight requests counts against reliability budget
items.recommendation: Separate local cancellation from reliability accounting. For example, add a recordReliability option to cancelAllPending(), call it with false from close(), and keep true for transport drops/timeouts/daemon errors.
items.reproduction: Create a client with driverIdentity and reliabilityBudget { failureThreshold: 1, windowMs: 60000, cooldownMs: 60000 }, connect to a fake transport that never responds, call request('session.list') and then close() before timeout. The close path records a failure; a new client sharing that ReliabilityBudget for the same identity will be quarantined.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing close() tests close after no pending request exists, and the reliability tests only exercise daemon timeouts and transport drops. There is no test for closing with pending requests under an identified driver budget.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that starts a hanging request with driverIdentity and failureThreshold: 1, calls close() before the request timeout, and asserts reliabilitySnapshot() remains empty or at least not quarantined.
items.minimumFixScope: DriverClient.close/cancelAllPending reliability accounting.

items.title: Standalone daemon command is not covered by process-level tests
items.recommendation: Add a small process-level integration test for the binary contract, at minimum covering help/usage and invalid invocation. If feasible on Unix, also spawn `anvil-intercept start` under an isolated temporary HOME/state directory, send SIGTERM, and assert it exits successfully.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Both included test files construct `IpcListener` or service harnesses in-process, bypassing `crates/anvil-intercept/src/main.rs` entirely.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Use `CARGO_BIN_EXE_anvil-intercept` or an `assert_cmd` equivalent to verify `anvil-intercept --help`, `anvil-intercept` without a subcommand, and a Unix-only `anvil-intercept start` smoke test that terminates via SIGTERM in a temporary environment.
items.minimumFixScope: Add binary-level integration coverage for `crates/anvil-intercept/src/main.rs`; no daemon library changes are required.

items.title: classifyIncoming treats malformed JSON-RPC envelopes as trusted responses or notifications
items.recommendation: Validate the full JSON-RPC shape before returning typed variants: id must be string, number, or null for responses; exactly one of result or error should be present; error must be an object with numeric code and string message; notifications should require a string method and no id. Return unknown for server requests unless the client explicitly supports a request kind.
items.reproduction: classifyIncoming({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', error: null }) returns { kind: 'response' }; a caller that branches on 'error' and passes it to errorFromResponse will dereference null. classifyIncoming({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'server-req', method: 'x' }) returns { kind: 'notification' } even though the id makes it a request, not a notification.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover valid success/error responses, valid notifications, non-object frames, missing jsonrpc, and notification-shaped frames without method. They do not cover malformed response bodies, result-plus-error envelopes, invalid id types, or method frames that also include id.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add classifyIncoming tests asserting unknown for {jsonrpc:'2.0', id:'req-1', error:null}, for response envelopes containing both result and error, for responses with non-string/non-number/non-null id values, and for {jsonrpc:'2.0', id:'server-req', method:'x'} unless a request kind is added.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/framing/jsonrpc.ts plus focused classifyIncoming tests in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/framing/jsonrpc.test.ts

items.title: Expired dedup entries are only purged when the same key is submitted again
items.recommendation: Purge stale cache entries independently of same-key lookup, for example by sweeping expired entries during submit, adding a bounded cache size, or scheduling expiry cleanup. Keep the cleanup deterministic for tests via the injected scheduler clock.
items.reproduction: Submit successful requests for many unique keys with dedupWindowMs set to a small value, advance the injected scheduler beyond the window, and do not submit those keys again. The stale entries remain retained because no code sweeps unrelated keys.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover same-key cache expiry after a later same-key submit, but they do not cover stale entries for keys that are never submitted again or assert cache size/memory behaviour.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a debouncer test using the manual scheduler that creates successful cache entries for multiple distinct keys, advances past dedupWindowMs, submits an unrelated key, and asserts stale entries are removed or bounded via a test-visible cache-size hook.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/debouncer.ts cache expiry logic plus a focused debouncer test

items.title: Cached diagnostics can be corrupted by caller mutation
items.recommendation: Do not expose cache-owned mutable structures. Clone ScanBufferResponse diagnostics before returning fresh and cached ValidateMidEditResult values, and ensure the cached value cannot be mutated through the fresh result. A deeper clone or immutable/readonly diagnostic contract is safer than only copying the array if consumers may mutate nested Diagnostic fields.
items.reproduction: Have the fake transport return one diagnostic, call validateMidEdit once, mutate the returned diagnostics array with result.diagnostics.length = 0, then call validateMidEdit again with the same uri/content inside the dedup window. The second call will return kind:"cached" with an empty diagnostics array even though the cached daemon response originally had one diagnostic.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked dedup tests assert cache hits and diagnostic counts, but they never mutate the first returned diagnostics before checking a cached result.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a validateMidEdit dedup test that mutates the diagnostics array returned by the initial diagnostics result, then repeats the same uri/content within the dedup window and asserts the cached result still contains the original daemon diagnostics.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/validate-mid-edit.ts result construction, with a focused regression in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/validate-mid-edit.test.ts

items.title: Zero-argument commands crash because action handlers expect a nonexistent second parameter
items.recommendation: Change zero-argument action callbacks to accept the command as the first parameter, for example `.action(async (cmd: Command) => { await runListCommand(cmd.optsWithGlobals() as ListOptions); })`, and make the same fix for audit and send-migration.
items.reproduction: Run `anvil-admin list --key test --json`, `anvil-admin audit --key test --json`, or `anvil-admin send-migration --key test --json`; each enters a zero-argument action where the second parameter is undefined and fails before calling the command implementation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing command tests call `runListCommand`, `runAuditCommand`, and `runSendMigrationCommand` directly. The only commander wiring tests build a local send-migration program that does not exercise `buildProgram()`'s actual action callback.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add `buildProgram()` wiring tests that register mocked command runners or parse these commands through `run()` and assert the relevant command implementation is invoked without a TypeError for `list`, `audit`, and `send-migration`.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the three zero-positional command action callback signatures in `apps/admin-cli/src/index.ts` and add wiring coverage in `apps/admin-cli/src/__tests__/index.test.ts`.

items.title: Expired cooldown is only cleared by isQuarantined, so recordFailure can immediately re-quarantine on stale failures
items.recommendation: Centralise expiry handling in a helper and call it from both recordFailure and isQuarantined before counting or checking state. When quarantinedUntil is expired, clear quarantinedUntil and failures before appending the new failure.
items.reproduction: Use failureThreshold=2, windowMs=60000, cooldownMs=1000. At t=0 call recordFailure(id) twice, then advance to t=1001 and call recordFailure(id) without first calling isQuarantined(id). The third call returns true and re-quarantines from one new failure because the two old timestamps are still within the 60s window.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The cooldown test advances past cooldown and calls isQuarantined, which is the only path that clears stale state. There is no test for recordFailure being the first budget method invoked after cooldown expiry.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that triggers quarantine, advances past cooldown while still inside windowMs, calls recordFailure(id) without a prior isQuarantined(id), and expects false plus a single failure in the snapshot.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/reliability/budget.ts and packages/anvil-driver-client/src/reliability/budget.test.ts

items.title: suppression/apply params omit the proposed comment and range required by the protocol
items.recommendation: Align AnvilSuppressionApplyParams with the authoritative wire contract by adding explicit proposed comment and range fields, or update the authoritative protocol if the intended contract is actually file/rule_id/reason. Then pin the full request payload shape in tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included protocol test only asserts the method string and never instantiates AnvilSuppressionApplyParams or checks the wire fields.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a suppression/apply request-shape test that serialises a representative params object including file, range, proposed comment, and reason, and asserts the exact snake_case wire keys.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/types.ts and packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/types.test.ts.

items.title: status/query params type contradicts the daemon route
items.recommendation: Change the status query request contract to model no params, or add a separate helper/overload that sends no params. Add the status result type separately if TS consumers need the DaemonStatusV1 shape.
items.reproduction: Call client.request(ANVIL_STATUS_QUERY, { workspace_root: '/tmp/wt' }) against the daemon's anvil/status/query route; the daemon rejects the params object.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/types.test.ts only checks the method-name constant and never constructs or sends AnvilStatusQueryParams.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a protocol type/fixture test asserting status query is sent without params, and a daemon parity fixture that rejects a params object for both query_status and anvil/status/query.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/types.ts, packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/index.ts if exports change, and packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/types.test.ts.

items.title: parseAgentTag accepts inherited properties as wire fields
items.recommendation: Reject arrays and require Object.hasOwn(value, 'driver_id'), Object.hasOwn(value, 'claimed_agent_id'), and Object.hasOwn(value, 'pid_starttime') before reading the values, or route through a shared asObject/own-field helper matching the stricter parser style used elsewhere.
items.reproduction:
const forged = Object.create({ driver_id: 'anvil-run', claimed_agent_id: 'attacker', pid_starttime: 1 });
parseAgentTag(forged); // currently returns an AgentTag instead of throwing
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The session tests cover null, primitives, arrays, plain missing fields, and malformed pid_starttime values, but they do not cover objects with prototype-supplied fields or a polluted Object.prototype.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parseAgentTag hostile-input test that passes Object.create({ driver_id: 'anvil-run', claimed_agent_id: 'attacker', pid_starttime: 1 }) and expects a TypeError mentioning driver_id or required own fields.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/session/types.ts plus packages/anvil-driver-client/src/session/types.test.ts

items.title: Backpressured sends can resolve successfully after the transport drops
items.recommendation: Track pending backpressure waiters as resolve/reject pairs and reject them from fireClose with anvil-daemon-transport-drop when the cause is peer or error. For local close, either reject pending sends as cancelled or wait for the write callback/drain before firing close, but do not report dropped writes as successful.
items.reproduction: Create a server that accepts a Unix socket connection and stops reading, call send() with a large payload until socket.write returns false, then close the server before the client receives drain. The pending send promise resolves via fireClose instead of rejecting with anvil-daemon-transport-drop.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The transport happy-path tests only send a small payload and wait for an echo; they never force socket.write to return false or close the connection while a send is pending. Windows tests cover only pipe-name validation and do not exercise send/drop behavior.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add Unix and Windows transport tests that mock or induce backpressure so socket.write returns false, close/error the socket before drain, and assert the pending send rejects with DriverClientError code anvil-daemon-transport-drop.
items.minimumFixScope: Update send/backpressure bookkeeping and fireClose handling in both UnixSocketTransport and WindowsNamedPipeTransport, plus targeted regression tests.

items.title: Windows pipe validation accepts arbitrary non-SID suffixes
items.recommendation: Validate the suffix against the Windows SID grammar expected by the daemon, for example S-1-... numeric components, or derive/obtain the current user SID and require an exact match where possible. Keep rejecting malformed suffixes before net.createConnection.
items.reproduction: Call validateWindowsPipeName('\\\\.\\pipe\\anvil-intercept-evil'); it returns without throwing, then WindowsNamedPipeTransport.connect would attempt to connect to that pipe name.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The Windows tests cover valid SID-like names, missing prefix, empty suffix, whitespace, and separators, but they do not assert that a non-SID suffix is rejected.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a validateWindowsPipeName test asserting that '\\\\.\\pipe\\anvil-intercept-not-a-sid' throws DriverClientError with code anvil-daemon-wrong-owner.
items.minimumFixScope: Tighten validateWindowsPipeName and extend windows.test.ts with malformed SID cases.

items.title: Protection claim parsers accept inherited/prototype fields as wire data
items.recommendation: Read only own properties for all wire fields. Add a small helper such as readOwn(obj, key) using Object.hasOwn(obj, key), and use it for schema_version, worktree_state, surfaces, identifier, state, and the optional protection_claim envelope field. Keep unknown own fields ignored for additivity.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing hostile test asserts the JSON.parse('__proto__') behaviour, but it never passes Object.create(...) or an object whose prototype has the required fields. It also does not cover inherited protection_claim on the validate_write envelope or inherited fields on surface entries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that parseProtectionClaim(Object.create({schema_version: PROTECTION_CLAIM_SCHEMA_VERSION, worktree_state: 'full', surfaces: []})) throws, parseSurfaceClaim(Object.create({identifier: 'mcp', state: 'participating'})) throws, and parseOptionalProtectionClaimFromValidateWrite(Object.create({protection_claim: validClaim})) returns undefined or throws according to the chosen own-field contract.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protection_claim/types.ts plus focused hostile-input tests in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protection_claim/types.test.ts

items.title: Air-gapped status verification can still attempt network refresh before running the local probe
items.recommendation: Special-case local/offline status verification before silent refresh, or add an auth-check mode that refuses/returns auth-required without refresh for commands documented as air-gapped. Then run the air-gapped harness without `ANVIL_DEV` against an isolated expired credential fixture with a refresh token.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included air-gapped test bypasses auth with `ANVIL_DEV=1`, so it verifies the status command body but not the global auth layer that runs first in production.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `air_gapped.rs` with a test that seeds isolated expired credentials containing a refresh token, runs `anvil --no-tui --json status --verify` through the network-blocked harness without `ANVIL_DEV`, and asserts the process does not attempt or hang on network refresh.
items.minimumFixScope: `crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs` auth pre-dispatch policy for documented local/offline commands plus the air-gapped credential fixture test.

items.title: JSON-mode entrypoint errors are emitted on stderr instead of stdout
items.recommendation: Route JSON-mode entrypoint envelopes to stdout, or introduce and document a single channel policy for all JSON responses and update command-level tests/contracts accordingly. Keep human diagnostics on stderr.
items.reproduction: Run a gated command without credentials in JSON mode, for example with an empty config home: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$(mktemp -d) ANVIL_NO_PROMPT=1 anvil --json status >out.json 2>err.json`. `out.json` is empty while `err.json` contains `{\"error\":\"authentication_required\"}`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included JSON tests either exercise commands that produce their own stdout JSON envelopes or bypass authentication with `ANVIL_DEV=1`; none assert the stdout/stderr contract for pre-dispatch auth failures or generic entrypoint errors.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that runs a gated command with `--json`, no credentials, and prompting disabled, then asserts stdout parses as the authentication error envelope and stderr contains no machine-readable primary response.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the JSON-mode error emission paths in `crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs` and add focused CLI integration coverage for pre-dispatch auth failure.

items.title: JSON-mode auth failures emit human text before the JSON error envelope
items.recommendation: Thread JSON/machine-output mode into auth evaluation, or make `check_auth` return a structured auth error without printing when `global.json` is set, leaving `main` as the single JSON error renderer.
items.reproduction: env -u ANVIL_DEV -u ANVIL_LICENSE ANVIL_NO_PROMPT=1 XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$(mktemp -d) cargo run -p eddacraft-anvil -- --json status 2>err; cat err
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included JSON-mode tests either use unauthenticated commands or set `ANVIL_DEV=1`, so they never exercise the gated auth-failure path in JSON mode.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that runs a gated command such as `anvil --json status` with isolated empty credentials and `ANVIL_NO_PROMPT=1`, then asserts stderr is exactly one parseable JSON object and contains no human auth guidance.
items.minimumFixScope: `crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs` auth error rendering plus one auth-failure JSON integration test.

items.title: Rejected DriverClientError instances do not carry the documented error discriminator
items.recommendation: Either add a readonly `error` alias to `DriverClientError` while preserving `code` for compatibility, or update the public comments to state that rejected Error instances use `code` and only `toJSON()` returns the `DriverError` wire shape.
items.reproduction: Catch any `DriverClient.request()` rejection, such as a timeout, and inspect `(err as any).error`; it is undefined while `(err as any).code` contains the discriminator.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests assert `.code` on rejected errors and assert `.toJSON().error` for serialised errors, but they never assert whether the rejected `DriverClientError` itself has the documented `.error` field.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an errors/client test that creates or catches a `DriverClientError` and verifies the chosen public contract explicitly: either `err.error === 'anvil-daemon-timeout'` if adding the alias, or no `.error` field plus documentation updated if `code` is the intended Error-instance contract.
items.minimumFixScope: `packages/anvil-driver-client/src/errors.ts` plus any tests or comments that pin the intended rejected-error shape.

items.title: Package build script points at a missing TypeScript config
items.recommendation: Either change the build script to `tsc -p tsconfig.json` or add a package-local `tsconfig.lib.json` that extends the existing config and is included in the package/project setup.
items.reproduction: From packages/anvil-driver-client, run `pnpm build`; TypeScript will try to load `tsconfig.lib.json` for this package.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise source behavior through Vitest; they do not invoke the package build script or assert that the configured TypeScript project file exists.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level build validation in CI/Nx for @eddacraft/anvil-driver-client, or a manifest smoke test that verifies the configured build tsconfig path exists.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/anvil-driver-client/package.json or add packages/anvil-driver-client/tsconfig.lib.json.

items.title: Benchmark reports can be overwritten by runs started in the same second
items.recommendation: Make report paths collision-resistant and non-clobbering, for example by including subsecond time plus process id or a UUID, and create the file with exclusive-create semantics so collisions fail instead of overwriting.
items.reproduction: Start two `cargo run -p anvil-bench --release -- graph_memory` processes from the same directory within the same Unix second; both compute the same `bench-results/stress-<timestamp>.json` output path and one report is lost.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise the CLI entrypoint or concurrent/same-second output path generation; existing report serialization tests do not validate collision behaviour for main.rs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration-style test around output path generation or a refactored `run` helper that forces the same timestamp for two runs and asserts the second run does not overwrite the first report.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the output filename/open mode in `crates/anvil-bench/src/main.rs`; factor path generation into a small testable helper if needed.

items.title: Dry-run preview token is never reused by the follow-up send
items.recommendation: Either add a `--preview-token <token>` send path and wire the dry-run token into the follow-up command, or remove the cross-invocation exact-set promise and make the UX explicit that only the same-process confirmation flow is pinned.
items.reproduction: Run `anvil-admin send-migration --source import` and review the dry-run output. Add or remove a matching waitlist recipient. Then run `anvil-admin send-migration --source import --no-dry-run --yes`; the second invocation creates and consumes a fresh preview token, so it targets the changed cohort rather than the original dry-run cohort.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests cover that a real send fetches a fresh preview and sends with that token, and that dry-run output surfaces a token, but they do not simulate separate dry-run and send invocations with recipient drift between them.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a commander or command-level test showing that a dry-run token can be supplied to a later real send and is the token posted to `/admin/send-migration`, without creating a second preview.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/admin-cli/src/commands/send-migration.ts`, `apps/admin-cli/src/index.ts`, and the send-migration tests.

items.title: Show output prints user-controlled panel fields without control-character sanitisation
items.recommendation: Export and reuse a shared text-cell sanitiser, or add a panel-specific sanitiser, and apply it to every interpolated user panel value before writing text output.
items.reproduction: Return a `/admin/user/:email` response where `user.name` or `user.notes` contains `\nstatus: active` or ANSI escape bytes, then run `anvil-admin show <email>` in text mode. The injected content is written directly in the USER panel.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The show tests only assert rendering for plain values and do not include newlines, tabs, or ANSI/control bytes in `name` or `notes`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a show-command text-mode test where `user.notes` contains newlines, tabs, and an ANSI escape byte, and assert the USER panel remains single-line per field with control bytes removed or collapsed.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/admin-cli/src/format.ts` to expose a sanitiser or helper, then use it in `apps/admin-cli/src/commands/show.ts` with a focused show test.

items.title: Root tsconfig lists files that TypeScript does not actually check
items.recommendation: Either remove the inert entries and keep this as a narrow TypeScript-only config check, or add a dedicated config-check tsconfig that enables `allowJs`/`checkJs` for eslint.config.mjs and uses the current E2E path, likely `apps/e2e/**/*` if root-level E2E files are still intended.
items.reproduction: `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --explainFiles | rg 'eslint\.config|jest\.config|e2e|vitest\.config|playwright\.config'` only reports vitest.config.ts and playwright.config.ts as matched by tsconfig.json.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this config. The existing root TypeScript invocation succeeds because TypeScript silently ignores the unmatched or unsupported include entries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small validation script or test that runs `tsc --explainFiles` for the root config and asserts every intentional include entry is either matched or explicitly documented as inert.
items.minimumFixScope: Update tsconfig.json include entries and, if JS config checking is intended, the compilerOptions needed to make eslint.config.mjs part of the checked program.

items.title: Root Vitest discovery can miss package __tests__ directories outside src
items.recommendation: Add an include pattern for package __tests__ directories that are not necessarily under src, or align the documented convention and config so there is a single discoverable test location. Consider disabling passWithNoTests at the root config if CI expects the root suite to find tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or config smoke tests are included that assert the Vitest include globs discover expected repository test locations.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small config-level test or CI smoke check that uses Vitest's resolved config/glob matching to assert packages/example/__tests__/sample.test.ts and packages/example/src/sample.test.ts are both discoverable.
items.minimumFixScope: vitest.config.ts include globs and, if retained intentionally, an explicit documented rationale for passWithNoTests.

items.title: Node type definitions exceed the supported runtime contract
items.recommendation: Either align @types/node to the minimum supported Node major, or raise the engines.node minimum if Node 25 APIs are intentionally allowed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise adapter parsing and serialization behavior; they do not verify package metadata consistency or run the suite against the minimum supported Node runtime.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package metadata validation test that checks the @types/node major does not exceed the minimum engines.node major, or add CI coverage on Node 22 that catches runtime use of newer Node APIs.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json devDependency or engines.node

items.title: Documented subpath API is not exported by the package
items.recommendation: Either change the public documentation to use only root exports that actually exist, or add explicit package exports for the documented subpaths with matching type declarations and update the submodule indexes to export the documented symbols or their current names. Prefer conditional export entries such as ./speckit, ./bmad, ./generic, and any intended utility entrypoint with both types and import targets.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included adapter tests import source files by relative paths, for example ../bmad/format-adapter.js and ../generic/format-adapter.js, so they bypass package.json exports and cannot catch a packaged-consumer import failure.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-boundary test that builds the adapters package, installs or resolves it as a consumer package, and dynamically imports @eddacraft/anvil-adapters/speckit, @eddacraft/anvil-adapters/bmad, @eddacraft/anvil-adapters/generic, and the documented utility entrypoint, asserting the documented named exports are present.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/package.json plus the affected submodule index files or README examples

items.title: Vercel ignore command does not quote rootDirectory or safely escape extraWatchPaths
items.recommendation: Build the ignore command with a single shell-escaping helper applied to rootDirectory, productionBranch, and every extraWatchPath, or validate all path inputs against a conservative repo-relative path pattern before interpolation. Add tests for metacharacters and spaces in rootDirectory and extraWatchPaths.
items.reproduction: Instantiate VercelApp with rootDirectory set to `apps/web; touch /tmp/pwned` or extraWatchPaths containing `docs/x' ; touch /tmp/pwned ; echo '` and inspect the generated Project ignoreCommand.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests cover shell metacharacter rejection for productionBranch only. They assert normal rootDirectory and extraWatchPaths fragments, but do not exercise metacharacters, whitespace, or embedded quotes in path arguments.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add VercelApp tests that reject or safely quote `rootDirectory: 'apps/web; echo bad'` and `extraWatchPaths: ["docs/a' ; echo bad"]`, then assert the generated ignoreCommand cannot execute additional shell tokens.
items.minimumFixScope: infra/src/components/vercel-app.ts plus infra/src/__tests__/vercel-app.test.ts

items.title: License verification accepts any ES256 token signed by the configured key
items.recommendation: Define the minimum license claim contract and pass issuer/audience requirements to jwtVerify, then validate required payload fields before returning valid: true.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests only cover cryptographic validity, expiry, malformed tokens, and wrong signatures. They do not include a signed token that is cryptographically valid but missing license-specific claims.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that signs a token with only generic claims and expects verifyLicense to return { valid: false }, plus a positive test for the required license claims.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/docs-shell/lib/jwt.ts and apps/docs-shell/lib/jwt.test.ts

items.title: Array undefined values break canonical JSON handling
items.recommendation: Handle undefined array elements explicitly, most likely by serialising them as 'null' to match JSON.stringify array semantics, or document and validate that arrays must not contain undefined.
items.reproduction: canonicalizeJSON([undefined]) throws TypeError instead of producing '[null]'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover top-level undefined and undefined object properties, but do not cover undefined values inside arrays.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a canonicalizeJSON test asserting canonicalizeJSON([1, undefined, 3]) is '[1,null,3]' if matching JSON.stringify semantics is desired.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the array branch in packages/anvil/core/src/crypto/hash.ts and add a focused regression test in packages/anvil/core/src/crypto/hash.test.ts.

items.title: Official SpecKit v2 import derives APS paths from unsanitized scenario titles
items.recommendation: Sanitize scenario-derived slugs to a safe identifier before building paths and validate every generated path with validateRelativePath. Return a conversion error or warning and skip the change when a safe path cannot be produced.
items.reproduction: Import a v2 spec containing a P1 scenario heading like '### P1: ../../outside'. buildProposedChanges will emit a file_create change with path 'src/../../outside/'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test is unrelated to SpecKit v2 imports and does not cover adversarial scenario titles or path traversal inputs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitImportAdapterV2 test with scenario titles containing '../', absolute path syntax, separators, and null bytes, asserting unsafe paths are rejected or normalized to safe identifiers that remain within the project root.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/speckit/import-v2.ts path derivation and v2 import regression tests.

items.title: SpecKit format round-trip rewrites serialized file paths to a generated placeholder
items.recommendation: Make serialize emit the path in a parser-supported form, for example backtick the heading path or add a first content line like Path: `src/foo.ts`; alternatively teach parseChangeSection/inferPathFromDescription to recognise the serializer's bare heading format.
items.reproduction: Serialize an APS plan with proposed_changes[0].path = 'src/foo.ts', then parse the returned markdown with SpecKitFormatAdapter.parse. The resulting change path becomes 'src/generated-file.ts' instead of 'src/foo.ts'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test is for the generic parser only and does not exercise SpecKit serialize-then-parse path preservation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitFormatAdapter round-trip test that serializes a plan with create, update, and delete paths, reparses it, and asserts each path is preserved.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/speckit/format-adapter.ts and/or packages/adapters/src/speckit/parser.ts plus a round-trip regression test.

items.title: SpecKit parser size guard can be bypassed with multi-byte input
items.recommendation: Use Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') or a shared byte-length guard before parsing SpecKit markdown.
items.reproduction: Call new SpecKitParser().parseSpecMarkdown('😀'.repeat(Math.floor((2 * 1024 * 1024) / 4) + 1)); the UTF-8 byte length is over 2 MiB while content.length remains under the current limit, so no maximum-size error is thrown.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test covers parseGeneric only. There is no equivalent SpecKitParser regression for multi-byte over-limit content.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitParser test mirroring the parseGeneric multi-byte case and assert parseSpecMarkdown throws /maximum size/.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/speckit/parser.ts plus a SpecKit parser size-guard test.

items.title: Public crate docs still describe shipped validation as deferred
items.recommendation: Update the `lib.rs` scope/out-of-scope section to reflect that hard-pinned validation is now part of the crate, and explicitly state that `parse_str`/`parse_file` parse only while callers that load operator config should call `validate_hard_pinned_classes` after parsing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover parse and validation behavior, but they do not verify that the public crate documentation matches the shipped API surface.
items.minimumFixScope: Documentation-only change in `crates/anvil-config/src/lib.rs`.

items.title: Testing entrypoint is not exported from the package
items.recommendation: Add explicit exports for ./testing and any intended nested testing subpaths, pointing to the built dist files and declarations, or remove the public module surface if these helpers are intentionally internal.
items.reproduction: From a consumer package, import '@eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/testing'; Node package resolution will fail with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED because ./testing is absent from package.json exports.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests import testing helpers through relative source paths, so they do not exercise package exports or consumer-style module resolution.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package export smoke test that builds @eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack and imports '@eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/testing' through Node/TypeScript package resolution.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/package.json exports map and a package-level import smoke test.

items.title: Provenance validation trusts embedded ref metadata after only checking IDs exist
items.recommendation: Fetch the observation/proposal records during validation and compare the embedded ref fields against the stored records. Use the stored proposal created_at for temporal ordering, and emit explicit mismatch issues for stale or inconsistent ref metadata.
items.reproduction: Store an observation and proposal with real timestamps, then validate a chain using the same IDs but altered ref timestamps and an altered ember_source.created_at that makes the temporal check pass; validateProvenanceChain will return valid unless another structural check fails.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked validator tests cover missing IDs and happy-path matching refs, but they do not include a case where IDs exist while session, kind, timestamp, proposal type, confidence, or created_at disagree with the stored records.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add validator tests where an existing observation ID is paired with the wrong session_id/timestamp and where an existing proposal ID is paired with a forged created_at; both should produce validation issues.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/testing/validators/provenance-chain.ts plus mismatch-focused validator tests.

items.title: Mock Edda supersedeMemory does not model superseded state or atomic failure
items.recommendation: Make supersedeMemoryImpl validate that the old memory exists and is active before creating the new memory, fail without mutating state when it cannot supersede, and mark the old memory status as superseded when the operation succeeds.
items.reproduction: Call createMockEddaPort().supersedeMemory(nonExistentId, input); the returned object contains old as null at runtime and the store contains the new memory. Or supersede an existing active memory and then call getStats(); superseded_count remains 0 while retired_count increases.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test file only covers provenance-chain validators. There are no included tests for Edda mock supersede behaviour, missing old IDs, or stats after superseding.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests for createMockEddaPort().supersedeMemory covering successful supersession status/stats and failure with an unknown old memory ID without creating a replacement.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/testing/mocks/edda.mock.ts and Edda mock tests.

items.title: The test-only any rule is enabled without any test-file guard
items.recommendation: Either scope the recommended config to test file globs, or make the rule skip non-test filenames unless explicitly configured otherwise.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: RuleTester cases do not set filenames for test and non-test files, so they only verify the AST selector behavior and not the documented file scope.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a valid case with `filename: 'src/index.ts'` and `const value = input as any;`, plus an invalid case with a test filename.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/rules/no-any-in-tests.ts, packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/index.ts if config scoping is chosen, and the no-any rule tests

items.title: Mock cleanup can be faked by comments or strings
items.recommendation: Detect an actual `CallExpression` for `vi.restoreAllMocks()` within the afterEach callback AST instead of scanning source text.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests include an afterEach without restore cleanup, but none where the required call appears only in a comment or string literal.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add invalid RuleTester cases where `vi.mock()` is used and afterEach contains only `// vi.restoreAllMocks()` or `const text = 'vi.restoreAllMocks()';`.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/rules/require-mock-cleanup.ts and its rule test file

items.title: CWD restoration accepts saving the directory after it has already changed
items.recommendation: Track source order: record the first non-restoration `process.chdir()` position and only accept cwd variables captured before that position as valid restoration targets.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover saving cwd and never restoring it, but not the false-negative case where cwd is saved after the initial `chdir`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an invalid case where `process.chdir('/tmp')` happens before `const originalCwd = process.cwd()` and then `process.chdir(originalCwd)` is called.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/rules/require-cwd-restoration.ts and its rule test file

items.title: Explain service first initialisation discards pre-registered templates
items.recommendation: Do not call clearTemplates from normal lazy initialisation. Make boundary template registration idempotent and reserve registry clearing for resetExplainService or explicit clearTemplates calls.
items.reproduction: Call resetExplainService(); registerTemplate({ ruleId: 'CUSTOM-001', render: ... }); then explainByRule('CUSTOM-001', { file: 'x.ts', line: 1 }). ensureTemplatesInitialised clears the registry and the result is null.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: template-loader.test.ts validates custom template registration in isolation, while explain-service.test.ts only asserts built-in architecture rules and retired AP-* behaviour. There is no test for a custom registered template surviving the service's first lazy initialisation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an explain-service test that registers a custom non-AP template before calling explainByRule, then asserts the custom explanation is returned after lazy initialisation.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/explain/explain-service.ts lazy initialisation plus one explain-service regression test.

items.title: similarCount can become negative when allWarnings omits the current warning
items.recommendation: Clamp similarCount at zero or compute it by excluding the current warning by identity or generated warning ID instead of blindly subtracting one.
items.reproduction: Call explainWarning with an ARCH-001 warning in src/a.ts and allWarnings containing only ARCH-001 warnings from other files, or an empty array. The generated context has similarCount = -1.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: explain-service.test.ts covers the happy path where allWarnings contains the current warning plus same-file siblings, so the subtraction produces a nonnegative count.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test for explainWarning(architectureWarning, []) and assert explanation.related.similarWarnings is 0 or undefined, never negative.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/explain/explain-service.ts buildContext and one regression test.

items.title: Top-level route wiring is mostly untested because tests mount sub-apps directly
items.recommendation: Add a small index-level smoke suite that imports the exported app and checks representative requests for every mounted surface under /api/v1, using lightweight mocked dependencies where needed. The assertions can target stable boundary behaviour such as 400 validation failures, 401 admin auth, health JSON, and a known CORS deny/allow case.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests intentionally mount routers directly, which is useful for route logic but does not cover the exported app's base path, route registration table, or global middleware stack.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Table-drive requests against the default export from ../index.js for /api/v1/auth/verify, /api/v1/auth/device/start, /api/v1/auth/otp/request, /api/v1/auth/session/refresh, /api/v1/auth/github/callback, /api/v1/admin/audit, /api/v1/waitlist, and /api/v1/health, asserting each route reaches the expected router instead of 404.
items.minimumFixScope: Add index-level integration tests; no production code change is required for this test-gap finding.

items.title: Global rate limiter can mask /health with 429 responses
items.recommendation: Exempt GET /health from the global limiter, or register /health before app.use('*', rateLimiter()) while preserving any desired logging/CORS behaviour. If health needs abuse protection, give it a separate, much higher operational-probe budget.
items.reproduction: Issue more than the global limiter's per-window allowance from the same forwarded IP to /api/v1/health, or consume the bucket on another route first and then request /api/v1/health. The health handler is bypassed and the response is 429 instead of the documented ok/degraded JSON.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not exercise /api/v1/health through the exported index app. The only index-level test is the CORS preflight case, while auth and admin tests mount sub-app routers directly.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Import ../index.js with getClient and verifySigningKey mocked, exhaust the global limiter from a fixed X-Forwarded-For value, then assert GET /api/v1/health still returns the health JSON with either 200 or 503 rather than 429.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/index.ts middleware ordering or path exemption, plus one index-level health regression test.

items.title: Queue updates outside join are unprotected and can lose entries under contention
items.recommendation: Use the same queue-file lock for every operation that mutates a queue file, including leave, cleanupTimedOut/getStatus cleanup, and cleanupAllTimedOut. Keep mutation helpers private behind a lock-held code path or split read-only status from locked cleanup.
items.reproduction: Have agent A queued. Start A.leave() and, between its loadQueue and atomicWriteJson/unlink, have agent B join the same queue. B's join writes [A,B], then A's stale leave can write [] or unlink the queue file, losing B's entry.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The queue-manager tests exercise join, leave, status, and priority sequentially in one process; they do not run concurrent join/leave/cleanup operations against the same queue file.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a concurrent queue mutation test that interleaves leave or timeout cleanup with another agent's join and asserts the newly joined entry remains in the queue.
items.minimumFixScope: Wrap all QueueManager queue-file mutations in the existing acquireFileLock protocol for the relevant queue path.

items.title: Concurrency subpath is not exported despite being the documented module entrypoint
items.recommendation: Add './concurrency' to packages/anvil/runtime/package.json exports with matching dist/concurrency/index.js and dist/concurrency/index.d.ts entries, and ensure the build emits that directory.
items.reproduction: Install or build the package with this package.json and run an ESM import for '@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency'; Node will reject the unexported subpath before loading dist/concurrency/index.js.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests import source files relatively and do not exercise the package exports map or the generated hook import path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level smoke test that builds the runtime package and dynamically imports '@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency', asserting exported symbols such as createConcurrencyContext and prepareCommitMsgHook are present.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the runtime package exports map and, if needed, build configuration so the concurrency entrypoint is emitted and importable.

items.title: Agent registry registration and heartbeat writes can overwrite concurrent agent state
items.recommendation: Protect all registry read-modify-write operations with a file lock, or replace whole-file writes with a compare-and-retry merge loop that detects the registry changed and reapplies the local mutation.
items.reproduction: Start two AgentManager instances for different agent IDs and call register() concurrently against the same workspace. If both load an empty or older registry before either save completes, the last writer's registry will contain only its own update.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked agent-manager test covers concurrent registrations or heartbeats; the included tests focus on atomic helpers, lock manager, queue manager, and git-agent utilities.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that concurrently registers multiple AgentManager instances sharing a workspace and asserts the final registry contains every agent with preserved heartbeat counts.
items.minimumFixScope: Add a registry lock around AgentManager mutations that call loadRegistry followed by saveRegistry.

items.title: Expired and stale lock takeover can grant the same lock to multiple agents
items.recommendation: Serialise forceAcquire with the same per-lock sentinel used by createLock, then re-read the lock after acquiring the sentinel and only take over if it is still expired/stale and not already held by another active agent.
items.reproduction: Create an expired lock file, then call acquire({type:'action', resource:'gate'}) concurrently from two LockManager instances with different agent IDs. Both calls can pass the expired check before either write completes and both can resolve with acquired true.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing expired-lock test only checks a sequential takeover by one second agent after expiry, so it cannot expose the double-acquisition race.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a race test that seeds an expired lock and starts two or more acquire calls in parallel, asserting exactly one result is acquired and the losers report the new holder.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the expired/stale takeover path in LockManager.acquire/forceAcquire to use an atomic sentinel and post-sentinel validation.

items.title: Nested section content is dropped during parsing
items.recommendation: Find the next heading at the same or higher level than the matched section instead of any line containing `##`. For these `##` section extractors, stop at the next `^##\s+` sibling heading, not `###` descendants, or switch to a markdown AST parser for section traversal.
items.reproduction:
Parse `# Plan

## Requirements

### Functional
- Add login
`; the requirements list is empty and `parseGeneric(...).proposed_changes` omits the item.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The parser test file only covers the byte-length guard and does not assert extraction behaviour for nested markdown sections.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add parser tests for `## Requirements` and `## Tasks` sections containing `###` subsections, asserting that list items under the child headings are preserved in the resulting APS plan.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `extractSectionBody` in `packages/adapters/src/generic/utils.ts` and add nested-section parser tests.

items.title: Plain requirements sections are parsed twice
items.recommendation: Make the header patterns mutually exclusive or deduplicate extracted requirement items after parsing. For example, use a single alternation that includes `Functional Requirements` and `Requirements`, or track matched section ranges before pushing items.
items.reproduction:
Parse `# Plan

## Requirements
- Add login
`; `extractRequirements` returns `['Add login','Add login']`, and `parseGeneric(...).proposed_changes` contains two equivalent changes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: `packages/adapters/src/generic/__tests__/parser.test.ts` only exercises the input byte-size guard, and serializer tests do not cover parser extraction or APS change generation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parser test asserting that a document with a single `## Requirements` section and one bullet produces exactly one requirement/change, while `## Functional Requirements` still parses once.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `extractRequirements` in `packages/adapters/src/generic/utils.ts` and add parser coverage in `packages/adapters/src/generic/__tests__/parser.test.ts`.

items.title: Package build script points at an uninspected tsconfig filename
items.recommendation: Either change the build script to `tsc -p tsconfig.json` or add the intended `tsconfig.lib.json` and keep it aligned with the package's emitted entrypoints.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/shared-storage build` in a checkout where `packages/shared/storage/tsconfig.lib.json` is absent; TypeScript will fail to find the configured project file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests run Vitest against source files and do not exercise the package build script or validate that the exported `dist` files can be produced.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level build verification in CI for `@eddacraft/shared-storage`, or include it in an existing workspace build check that fails when the configured tsconfig is missing.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `packages/shared/storage/package.json` or add the missing package build tsconfig.

items.title: BundleManager signature_key cannot verify downloaded bundles because the signature is never downloaded
items.recommendation: Add an explicit signature URL/source to BundleConfig and download it before verification, or remove this detached-signature path and integrate BundleVerifier against OPA .signatures.json manifests after extraction.
items.reproduction: Configure BundleManager with verifySignatures true and a bundle with signature_key against any valid test tarball. downloadBundle fails with 'Signature verification failed' because `${tempFile}.sig` was never created.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The BundleManager test fixture disables verifySignatures globally and has no test for signature_key success or failure modes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test server endpoint for bundle.tar.gz.sig, configure signature_key/signatureUrl, and assert a correctly signed bundle succeeds while a missing signature fails with a precise error.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleConfig signature contract and BundleManager.downloadBundle signature acquisition/verification flow.

items.title: Bundle redirects bypass the HTTPS policy and can leak auth headers
items.recommendation: Resolve redirects against the current URL, enforce HTTPS for every redirect except the same localhost development allowance, cap redirect depth, and do not forward Authorization or caller-supplied sensitive headers across origin changes.
items.reproduction: Serve an HTTPS bundle URL that responds 302 Location: http://attacker.example/bundle.tar.gz, configure auth.token_env, and call downloadBundle. The recursive request will use the http module and include Authorization.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The redirect test uses localhost and only asserts success. It does not cover HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade, cross-origin redirects, or auth/header forwarding.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a redirect test that starts from an HTTPS-capable mock or stubs downloadFile response handling, redirects to http://non-localhost, and asserts downloadBundle fails without sending Authorization.
items.minimumFixScope: Redirect handling in BundleManager.downloadFile.

items.title: Policies with the same basename overwrite each other during evaluation
items.recommendation: Preserve a stable relative path or generate collision-free temp filenames from the policy path/package. Detect duplicate policy names if name uniqueness is an intended contract and return a load/evaluation error instead of overwriting.
items.reproduction: Create .anvil/policies/team_a/rules.rego and .anvil/policies/team_b/rules.rego with different packages/rules. loadPolicies returns two LoadedPolicy objects both named 'rules'; evaluate writes both to tempDir/rules.rego, leaving only the second file for OPA.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The recursive loader test uses unique basenames, and the executor multiple-policy test also uses unique names. No test creates duplicate basenames in different directories.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an evaluation test with two LoadedPolicy entries sharing name 'rules' but different content and assert both are passed to OPA via distinct temp files or that the duplicate is rejected explicitly.
items.minimumFixScope: PolicyLoader naming contract and OPAExecutor.setupTempDirectory temp file naming.

items.title: ANVIL_OPA_PATH returns an executable even when version verification fails
items.recommendation: Check the verifyVersion result for ANVIL_OPA_PATH and throw a descriptive version-mismatch error when it is false, matching the cached/system binary handling.
items.reproduction: Set ANVIL_OPA_PATH to an executable that prints 'Version: 0.1.0' and construct OPABinaryManager for version 1.16.1. ensureBinary still returns that path.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The ANVIL_OPA_PATH test only asserts that existing paths are considered before 'file not found' errors. It does not assert rejection for an executable with the wrong OPA version.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with an executable mock that prints Version: 0.1.0 and assert ensureBinary rejects when the configured version is 1.16.1.
items.minimumFixScope: OPABinaryManager.ensureBinary env override branch.

items.title: Advertised Ed25519 bundle signatures always fail verification
items.recommendation: Implement Ed25519 using the one-shot crypto.verify(null, dataBuffer, publicKey, signature) API, or remove Ed25519 from SignatureAlgorithm and DEFAULT_ALLOWED_ALGORITHMS until it is supported.
items.reproduction: Generate an Ed25519 key pair/signature for a valid files array, configure a PublicKeyConfig with algorithm 'Ed25519', and call verifyBundle. The Ed25519 branch throws during createVerify('ed25519') and the bundle is rejected.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The signature tests generate RSA and P-256 EC key pairs and cover RS256/ES256, but there is no Ed25519 key generation or successful Ed25519 verification case.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a valid Ed25519 signed bundle test using generateKeyPairSync('ed25519') and crypto.sign(null, Buffer.from(signedData), privateKey), expecting verifyBundle to succeed.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleVerifier.verifySignature Ed25519 branch and associated tests.

items.title: Bundle verification accepts extra unsigned files in a signed bundle
items.recommendation: After validating a signature block, enumerate all relevant bundle contents and require exact coverage by the signed file list, excluding only the signature manifest and explicitly allowed metadata. Reject duplicate names and empty file lists.
items.reproduction: Create a bundle directory with signed policy.rego in .signatures.json and an additional malicious.rego not listed in the manifest. Sign the manifest files array for policy.rego only. verifyBundle returns verified=true.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing verifier tests cover valid single-file and multi-file manifests where the manifest exactly matches the files they created, but they do not add an unsigned extra file and assert rejection.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that signs policy.rego, writes unsigned_extra.rego beside it, and expects verifyBundle(...).verified to be false with an unsigned-file error.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleVerifier.verifySignatureBlock plus a helper to enumerate and compare bundle file coverage.

items.title: Bundle names can escape the cache directory and remove or write arbitrary paths
items.recommendation: Validate bundle names at add/constructor time as a safe slug with no separators, dot segments, or absolute paths. Also resolve every derived path and reject it unless it is inside the resolved cacheDir.
items.reproduction: Configure a bundle with name '../victim' and a valid localhost test bundle, using a cacheDir beside an existing victim directory. Calling downloadBundle('../victim') resolves bundleDir outside the cache and can remove/recreate that directory.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The bundle manager tests use simple names such as 'bundle1', 'redirect-bundle', and 'checksum-bundle'; they never exercise path separators or dot segments in bundle names.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BundleManager test that attempts to add/download/invalidate a bundle named '../outside' and asserts the operation is rejected and no path outside cacheDir is touched.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleManager bundle-name validation plus resolved-cache containment checks for bundleDir, tempFile, and invalidate paths.

items.title: Public observation emitters pass sensitive command, prompt, and error text through without any redaction step
items.recommendation: Apply a central sensitive-data validation/redaction step before service.emit for all free-text and path-like fields, or reject observations containing configured secret patterns. Keep the policy consistent across action, human_input, and error emitters.
items.reproduction: Pass a command such as `deploy --token=secret` to emitActionExecuted or an error_message containing an Authorization header to emitError; the captured observation contains the secret verbatim.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for these emitters, and the included code has no assertion or guard showing that sensitive fields are scrubbed before emission.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests with representative secrets in command, prompt, decision, user_identifier, error_message, and partial_state_description, then assert the emitted observations are redacted or rejected according to the package policy.
items.minimumFixScope: The emitter layer for action, human input, and error observations, with shared sanitisation to avoid inconsistent field coverage.

items.title: ActionDetails type allows semantically incomplete action observations
items.recommendation: Make ActionDetails a discriminated union keyed by action_type, or add runtime validation before emission so each action type requires its minimum meaningful fields.
items.reproduction: Compile a caller that invokes emitActionExecuted with `{ action_type: 'command', details: { working_directory: '/tmp' }, ... }`; this satisfies the declared interface and emits a command action with no command.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included, and there is no compile-time fixture or runtime test demonstrating that invalid action/detail combinations are rejected.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add TypeScript type tests or runtime unit tests covering each action_type, including negative cases where required type-specific fields are omitted.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/kindling-integration/src/emitters/action-emitter.ts input type and validation path for emitActionExecuted.

items.title: Human input emitter returns an ID that is never attached to the emitted observation
items.recommendation: Either add the generated ID to the HumanInputObservation contract and emitted payload, or stop generating/returning an ID and update the API documentation to return a real correlation key.
items.reproduction: Call emitHumanInput with a mock KindlingService that captures the observation; the returned UUID will not appear anywhere in the emitted human_input payload.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata includes no linked tests, and no included test asserts that the returned human input ID is present in the emitted observation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test for emitHumanInput using a fake KindlingService and assert that the returned ID is present in the emitted observation under the contract-approved ID field.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/kindling-integration/src/emitters/human-input-emitter.ts plus the human_input observation contract/schema if an input_id field does not already exist.

items.title: MemoryStore can delete files outside the storage root through a crafted index path
items.recommendation: Validate index entry paths before filesystem operations using the same root containment rules as VersionTracker.resolveTrackedPath, and reject absolute paths, empty segments, and '..'. Prefer a private resolveStorageRelativePath helper used by readMemoryFromEntry, saveMemory, and deleteMemory.
items.reproduction: Create an index.yaml entry for an existing memory id whose path is '../victim.txt' or an absolute path, then call saveMemory with the same id and a type that changes the expected path, or call deleteMemory(id). The store will unlink/rmSync the indexed target outside the storage root if it exists.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: MemoryStore tests verify invalid memory IDs are rejected before write and that normal type changes remove the old in-root file, but they do not create a hostile index.yaml path or assert storage-root containment during delete/update cleanup.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Write an index.yaml with a valid memory id and path '../outside.yaml', create that outside file, then assert saveMemory/deleteMemory throws and the outside file still exists.
items.minimumFixScope: MemoryStore path resolution for index-derived paths plus MemoryIndexEntry path validation/regression tests.

items.title: Failed supersede can silently convert an active memory into a retired memory
items.recommendation: On replacement save failure, restore the original oldMemory exactly, or make the API explicitly return/commit a failure retirement state only after a separate caller-confirmed operation. If exact rollback can fail, report that the memory may remain superseded, but do not intentionally downgrade it to retired as the normal fallback.
items.reproduction: Use a store whose second saveMemory call throws. Call supersedeMemory for an active memory. The call rejects, but getMemory(oldId) returns status 'retired' rather than the original active memory.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current test asserts the problematic fallback retirement, so tests cover the behaviour but not the safer failure contract that a failed supersede should leave the active memory active.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Change the failed replacement test to expect the old memory to equal its original active object after supersedeMemory rejects, including status, evolution, and timestamps.
items.minimumFixScope: EvolutionService.supersedeMemory failure path and its corresponding test expectations.

items.title: Package typecheck target combines incompatible TypeScript emit flags
items.recommendation: Remove `emitDeclarationOnly` from this app tsconfig, or split declaration emission into a separate build tsconfig/target and keep the typecheck config compatible with `tsc --noEmit`.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/docs-shell typecheck` or `pnpm exec nx run docs-shell:typecheck`; TypeScript should report that `emitDeclarationOnly` cannot be specified with `noEmit`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Vitest tests exercise runtime helpers only. They do not run the package or Nx typecheck target, so they would not catch a compiler option conflict.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add the docs-shell typecheck target to CI or a workspace validation test that invokes `pnpm exec nx run docs-shell:typecheck`.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/docs-shell/tsconfig.json

items.title: Root barrel export has no direct coverage
items.recommendation: Add a focused package-entrypoint test that imports from packages/aps/src/index.js and asserts the expected public symbols are present, ideally including representative symbols from parser, loader, filter, validator, state, types, and templates.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests validate each module's local index or implementation file, but none imports packages/aps/src/index.ts or the package root export surface declared by package.json.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create packages/aps/src/index.test.ts importing from './index.js' and asserting that parseDocument, loadPlan, filterPlan, validatePlanningDoc, TaskLocker, and template generators are exported as functions/classes as expected.
items.minimumFixScope: Add a root barrel export-surface test; no production code change is required unless that test exposes missing or conflicting exports.

items.title: send-migration can report failure after emails were already sent
items.recommendation: Do not let the post-send audit insert mask completed delivery. Either make this audit write best-effort and return the send summary with an auditError marker, or persist an auditable pending/send-start row before delivery and update it after delivery without changing the already-completed response semantics.
items.reproduction: Mock consumeSendMigrationSnapshot and findWaitlistBySource to return a valid unchanged snapshot, mock sendWaitlistMigration to resolve sent:true, and mock insertAuditLog to reject. POST /admin/send-migration with dryRun:false and a previewToken returns 500 after sendWaitlistMigration has already been called for the recipients.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests cover drift rejection, duplicate-token rejection, full send success, and email-provider partial failures, but none make insertAuditLog fail after successful sends.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a /admin/send-migration real-send test where insertAuditLog rejects after sendWaitlistMigration succeeds; assert the response still returns the send summary and that recipients are not re-sent within that request.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/admin.ts send-migration real-send audit handling plus the admin route test suite.

items.title: Graded-scope licence behaviour is only partially covered
items.recommendation: Add decoded-JWT assertions for preview/beta scopes on /auth/verify, /auth/license/refresh, /auth/device/poll, and /auth/github/callback when findActiveScopesForUser returns ['preview','beta'].
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Those tests use the default ['beta'] mock or only check that the returned licence is syntactically a JWT; they do not assert the scopes claim for graded entitlements.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: For each affected route, mock findActiveScopesForUser to return ['preview','beta'], decode the returned licence with jose decodeJwt, and assert claims.scopes equals ['preview','beta'].
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/auth.test.ts, apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/auth-device.test.ts, and apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/auth-github.test.ts.

items.title: postbuild runtime probe requires an undeclared transitive package
items.recommendation: Make the probe depend only on declared package entrypoints, for example require('resend') or the exact public path that triggers resend's svix require chain, or add svix as an explicit direct dependency of @eddacraft/anvil-api if the script intentionally owns that contract.
items.reproduction: In a clean strict pnpm install where transitive dependencies are not hoisted into apps/anvil-api/node_modules, run pnpm --dir apps/anvil-api build; the postbuild step executes node scripts/check-runtime-cjs.cjs and require('svix') can fail before validating the intended uuid CJS compatibility path.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/migrate.test.ts only imports and exercises ../db/migrate.js helpers; it does not run scripts/check-runtime-cjs.cjs, the postbuild lifecycle, or package dependency isolation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level script test that runs node scripts/check-runtime-cjs.cjs in the app package after install/build and asserts it succeeds without relying on undeclared transitive hoisting.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/anvil-api/scripts/check-runtime-cjs.cjs and, if choosing the direct-dependency approach, apps/anvil-api/package.json.

items.title: Hash validation status is dropped by the public validate result
items.recommendation: Propagate hashResult.hashValidated from validateHash into the final result whenever hash validation was requested. Consider preserving non-fatal warning information separately from invalidating errors so skipped validation remains visible without making schema-valid plans fail unless that is the intended policy.
