items.reproduction: Create a new APSValidator without setHashValidator(), call validate(validPlan, { validateHash: true }), and inspect result.hashValidated. It is undefined even though validateHash would have returned hashValidated: false.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing hash tests assert valid and summary contents only; they do not check result.hashValidated for skipped, passed, or failed validation through APSValidator.validate().
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that call validate(plan, { validateHash: true }) with no hash validator and with a real/mock hash validator, asserting hashValidated is false for skipped validation and true for successful validation.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/validation/aps-validator.ts plus validation tests for the public validate() result contract.

items.title: Plan-based file filtering uses a different path form than planless filtering
items.recommendation: Move the plan-based filter application after fullPath is computed and pass the absolute path to match normaliseTargetFiles. If callers need to filter raw plan paths, add a separate option or document that contract explicitly.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and repository search found no runtime test importing getFilesFromContext or normaliseTargetFiles.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a vitest case for getFilesFromContext where targetFiles ['src/a.ts'] and plan.proposed_changes [{ type: 'file_update', path: 'src/a.ts', ... }] both include the same file when using a filter that expects absolute paths under workspace_root.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/types/gate.types.ts plus focused tests for planless and plan-based filter parity

items.title: Direct contracts import is not declared in package metadata
items.recommendation: Add "@eddacraft/anvil-contracts": "workspace:*" to apps/e2e/package.json dependencies if it is an intended direct E2E surface.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The smoke test proves the import resolves in the current repository layout, but it does not verify manifest completeness.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package manifest consistency check that fails when apps/e2e/src/**/*.ts imports an @eddacraft/* workspace package not listed in package.json dependencies or devDependencies.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/e2e/package.json

items.title: API client throws on non-JSON responses
items.recommendation: Read the body once with res.text(), then parse it as JSON only when appropriate, such as when the content-type is JSON and the text is non-empty. Return the raw text on parse failure.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included API tests mostly call app.request() directly and do not exercise createApiClient against a non-JSON response.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a helper test using a Hono route that returns c.text('not json', 500) and assert createApiClient().get() returns status 500 with body 'not json' without throwing.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/e2e/src/helpers/api-client.ts

items.title: Schema compatibility test compares core to itself
items.recommendation: Import the first schema/createPlan set from @eddacraft/anvil-contracts and keep the aliased comparison imports from @eddacraft/anvil-core.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing assertions pass because both sides of the comparison are the same module.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: After correcting the imports, keep an assertion that createPlan, APS_SCHEMA_VERSION, and APSPlanSchema parse behaviour match between @eddacraft/anvil-contracts and @eddacraft/anvil-core.

items.title: Context bundles can omit scope-matched tasks outside scope-matched modules
items.recommendation: Keep module and task sets coherent for bundle generation. Either have filterPlan include modules containing any filtered task, or have the bundle builders derive the displayed module set from filtered.tasks' containing modules as well as filtered.modules.
items.reproduction: Create or use a plan where module A has scope PROD and contains a task with scopes ['PROD', 'AUTH']; call filterPlan(plan, { scopes: ['AUTH'] }) and then buildContextBundleJSON/buildContextBundleText. The task is present in filtered.tasks but absent from the rendered module task lists unless module A itself has metadata.scope AUTH.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The scope tests assert only that filtered.tasks match the scope predicate. The context bundle tests check the AUTH module and that tasks exist, but not that every filtered task is represented in the bundle output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fixture task in a non-AUTH module with AUTH in its scopes, filter by AUTH, and assert the JSON/Text bundle includes that task and its containing module or otherwise represents it explicitly.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/filter/index.ts or packages/aps/src/filter/context-bundle.ts, plus filter.test.ts coverage for cross-module scope task rendering.

items.title: Status criteria are not reported by context bundles
items.recommendation: Add statuses to ContextBundleJSON.filter and include criteria.statuses in both the JSON filter object and Markdown filterParts.
items.reproduction: Call filterPlan(plan, { statuses: ['locked'] }) and pass the result to buildContextBundleJSON or buildContextBundleText. The tasks are status-filtered, but bundle.filter has no statuses field and the Markdown banner has no status entry.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The filter-criteria bundle test covers scopes and tags only. There are no status-filter tests for filterPlan or either context bundle format.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that filter with { statuses: ['locked'] } and assert bundle.filter.statuses equals ['locked'] and the Markdown output contains 'statuses: locked'.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/filter/context-bundle.ts and packages/aps/src/filter/filter.test.ts.

items.title: Parser accepts governance tables that are not immediately after the H1
items.recommendation: Replace collectTablesAfterH1 with logic that inspects the immediate top-level siblings after the H1, allowing only ignorable whitespace/html comments if the convention permits them, and requiring the metadata table followed directly by the relationships table.
items.reproduction: Call parseDocGovernance on Markdown containing '# Title', then a paragraph such as 'intro text', then otherwise valid metadata and relationships tables. The current collectTablesAfterH1 loop skips the paragraph and returns the later tables instead of throwing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The happy-path test places both tables directly after the H1, and the missing-table tests use documents with no later valid tables. There is no negative case with valid tables appearing later after intervening prose or a second heading.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test where '# Title' is followed by prose before valid governance tables and assert parseDocGovernance throws a ParseError for missing/non-immediate metadata. Add a second case where the relationships table is separated from metadata by prose if that is also forbidden.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/docs-meta/src/parser/parse-metadata.ts and packages/docs-meta/src/parser/parse-metadata.test.ts

items.title: rule panic isolation is not valid in release builds with panic=abort
items.recommendation: Either build the daemon/rule-execution path with panic="unwind" if catch_unwind is the intended boundary, or move rule execution behind a process boundary so aborting rules cannot terminate the daemon. Add the documented multi-process release fixture before treating the contract as covered.
items.reproduction: Run the daemon in a release profile configured with panic="abort" and install a rule equivalent to panicking_rule_service; sending rule_panic_request aborts the daemon process instead of returning the unwind-mode empty diagnostics response.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current Rust fixture explicitly pins only panic="unwind" behaviour under cargo test and documents the panic="abort" release path as an unimplemented follow-up.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a multi-process release-profile test that starts the daemon with a panicking rule and asserts the expected release contract, either no daemon abort or a controlled child-process failure with daemon survival.
items.minimumFixScope: Release profile or rule-execution isolation strategy, plus the midedit_contract release-mode regression fixture.

items.title: stale PID recovery can remove a newly-created live PID file
items.recommendation: Serialise PID-file recovery and daemon ownership with an actual lock, or make recovery remove only the exact file identity that was inspected. On Unix, hold a lock file or locked open PID file across recovery and daemon lifetime; do not rely on a read/status/remove/create sequence alone.
items.reproduction: Start two run_foreground instances concurrently against the same stale PID file, with recovery interleaved so both read the stale record before either remove_file call completes. The second remover can unlink the first starter's replacement PID file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover stale recovery and that Drop preserves an already-replaced PID file, but they do not run two stale-recovery attempts concurrently or force the interleaving between stale read, first recreate, and second remove.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Unix test that uses two coordinated tasks/processes and an injected recovery hook to pause both after stale-status detection, then lets one recreate the PID file before the other attempts removal. Assert the live replacement is not removed and only one daemon proceeds.
items.minimumFixScope: PidFileGuard acquisition and stale PID recovery logic in crates/anvil-intercept/src/lib.rs, plus a targeted concurrent stale-recovery regression test.

items.title: Exported PACKAGE_VERSION is stale relative to the package manifest
items.recommendation: Derive PACKAGE_VERSION from the release source of truth during build, or update the constant whenever package.json is bumped. Add a test that asserts the exported constant matches the manifest version.

items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise config and contract modules directly, mostly through ./config.js or ./contracts/*.js imports. None of the included tests imports packages/edda-stack/src/index.ts or asserts PACKAGE_VERSION.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a root index test that imports PACKAGE_VERSION and reads packages/edda-stack/package.json, then expects PACKAGE_VERSION to equal the manifest version.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/edda-stack/src/index.ts and add a focused root index test.

items.title: Package test script is likely to fail with no test files
items.recommendation: Add focused schema tests for the exported contracts so `vitest run` has real coverage. If this package is intentionally testless, make that explicit with `--passWithNoTests`, but that would leave the contract behaviour unverified.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no tests, and none were provided as evidence to exercise this package script or the schema contracts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests covering representative successful and rejected parses for InviteResponseSchema, SendMigrationResponseSchema, AuditResponseSchema, and ShowResponseSchema.

items.title: Send migration discriminator is not enforced on real-send responses
items.recommendation: Make the union discriminator explicit, for example by using a discriminated union with an explicit false/absent branch or by making SendResponseSchema reject a `dryRun` field with `.strict()` or an equivalent refinement.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were included for malformed send-migration payloads or discriminator edge cases.

items.minimumFixScope: Update SendResponseSchema or SendMigrationResponseSchema in packages/shared/admin-contracts/src/index.ts and add schema regression tests.

items.title: Package build script points at an unowned TypeScript config
items.recommendation: Either change the build script to `tsc -p tsconfig.json` or add and own a committed `tsconfig.lib.json` that intentionally extends the package config.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or build validation were included for this feature, so the package script path is not exercised.

items.title: Common subpath is blocked by the package exports map
items.recommendation: Either add an explicit `./common` export with matching JS and declaration paths, or remove/privatise the common barrel and expose the intended common API through the root entrypoint consistently.

items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package export smoke test that builds the adapters package and verifies the intended public imports, including `@eddacraft/anvil-adapters/common` if it is meant to be public.

items.title: Linked registry tests do not cover the common registry implementation
items.recommendation: Add focused tests for `packages/adapters/src/common/registry.ts`, or remove the duplicated common registry if the base registry is the only supported implementation.

items.title: inferBaseline save:false still writes and can overwrite the architecture baseline
items.recommendation: Either make save:false truly non-persistent by creating the baseline value without BaselineManager.create, or remove/rename the save option and update documentation/tests to make the write explicit. If preserving current behaviour, add a separate dry-run API so callers can infer without disk mutation.

items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current test asserts that save:false still persists, so it protects the implementation quirk rather than the documented API contract or no-overwrite expectation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Change the save:false test to pre-create .anvil/architecture.json, call inferBaseline(..., { save: false }), and assert the original file content is unchanged while the returned baseline is populated.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/analyzer.ts plus the inferBaseline tests.

items.title: Dependency-cruiser regex generation can emit invalid regex for adjacent metacharacters
items.recommendation: Remove the global flag from REGEX_METACHARACTERS or replace .test(char) with a stateless check. Add coverage for adjacent metacharacters and verify the generated path regex is constructible and matches the literal path.
items.reproduction: Generate a DC config with a layer pattern like src/(generated)/** and then construct new RegExp(rule.from.path). The '(' can be left unescaped after a prior metacharacter match, yielding an invalid or incorrect regex.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current metacharacter test only uses src/utils+helpers/**, where the metacharacter is isolated; it never checks consecutive metacharacters or constructs a RegExp from the generated output for those cases.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a dc-generator test using patterns ['src/(generated)/**/*.ts'] and assert new RegExp(rule.from.path) does not throw, matches 'src/(generated)/file.ts', and does not match 'src/generated/file.ts'.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/dc-generator.ts and the dc-generator test file.

items.title: Pattern compiler scripts rely on undeclared tsx binary
items.recommendation: Declare tsx as a devDependency in the package that owns these scripts, or rewrite the scripts to run compiled JavaScript through node after build. Keep the dependency explicit wherever the script is invoked in CI/release.
items.reproduction: On a clean install without a global or transitive tsx binary, run pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-core patterns:check; the script cannot resolve tsx.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise compilePatterns directly through Vitest; they do not execute package scripts in an environment with only declared dependencies available.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-script smoke check in CI or a release validation step that runs pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-core patterns:check after a clean install.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/package.json.

items.title: Duration formatting can render impossible 60-second remainders
items.recommendation: Round or floor the total seconds first, then derive minutes and seconds from that normalised total, e.g. const seconds = Math.round(num); const mins = Math.floor(seconds / 60); const rem = seconds % 60.
items.reproduction: Render MetricCard with { label: 'Duration', value: '119.9', format: 'duration' }; displayed becomes 1m 60s.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests validate specs but do not render MetricCard or exercise duration formatting edge cases; the fixture duration value is an integer below 60 seconds.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a MetricCard rendering/unit test covering fractional duration values around minute boundaries, such as 119.9 seconds, and assert the seconds remainder is never 60.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/libs/render/src/components/metric-card.tsx plus a focused component or formatting regression test.

items.title: Percentage targeting accepts out-of-range values
items.recommendation: Constrain percentage operator values to the intended numeric range, typically 0 through 100 inclusive, and report the issue at path ['value'].
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover a valid numeric value and reject a string value, but they do not cover boundary or out-of-range numeric values such as -1 or 101.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add TargetingConditionSchema cases asserting that percentage values below 0 and above 100 are rejected, and that 0, 25, and 100 are accepted if those are the intended bounds.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.ts and packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.test.ts

items.title: Targeting rules can reference undeclared variants
items.recommendation: In FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.check, derive the set of declared variant keys and reject every targeting rule whose variant is not in that set, reporting the path for the offending targeting entry.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover defaultVariant referential integrity and valid targeting rules, plus empty targeting variant strings, but they never assert that a non-empty targeting variant must reference an existing variant key.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema test with targeting: [{ conditions: [...], variant: 'nonexistent' }] and expect safeParse(...).success to be false.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.ts and packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.test.ts

items.title: Public declarations reference json-schema types without declaring the type package
items.recommendation: Either add the required JSON Schema type package as a direct dependency for published consumers, or avoid exporting a declaration that depends on external json-schema typings by using a local/bundled JSON schema type.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise runtime schema behaviour but do not build the package and consume its emitted declarations from an isolated install.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level declaration-consumer smoke test that builds @eddacraft/anvil-contracts, installs or links it into an isolated fixture, and runs tsc against an import of generateJSONSchema.

items.title: DEBUG=anvil:api enables every debug namespace
items.recommendation: Make isDebugEnabled namespace-aware. Treat anvil:* as global, ANVIL_DEBUG=1/true as global if intended, and require DEBUG to contain the exact namespace such as anvil:auth-session before logging that namespace.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no included tests for debug namespace selection, and the current tests never set DEBUG or call createDebugger with different namespaces.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that set DEBUG=anvil:api and assert createDebugger('api') logs while createDebugger('auth-device') and createDebugger('auth-session') do not, then set DEBUG=anvil:* and assert all namespaces log.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/lib/debug.ts and a focused debug namespace test.

items.title: Audience move can drop a contact from both audiences on partial failure
items.recommendation: Prefer add-then-remove semantics for the move, and only remove from the waitlist after the beta audience add succeeds or is known to already exist. Consider returning a structured result so callers can observe partial failures if audience state matters operationally.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included linked tests do not exercise audience.ts or simulate partial Resend failures during a waitlist-to-beta move.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an audience test with a mocked Resend client where waitlist removal succeeds and beta create rejects, then assert the implementation either does not remove first or reports a partial failure instead of silently completing.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/lib/audience.ts plus a mocked audience unit test.

items.title: Structured debug payloads bypass redaction
items.recommendation: Sanitise structured data before logging, for example by recursively redacting known sensitive keys and string values or by serialising with a redacting replacer before passing to console.debug. Add coverage for nested objects, arrays, Error objects, bearer tokens, anvil_beta tokens, and GitHub/Resend-style secrets.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover token, device-code, email waitlist confirmation, feature flags, and licence signing, but there is no debug utility test exercising structured data redaction.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a debug.test.ts that sets ANVIL_DEBUG=1, spies on console.debug, calls createDebugger('auth-session') with { authorization: 'Bearer abc.def.ghi', token: 'anvil_beta_' + 'a'.repeat(43) }, and asserts no raw secret substring reaches the log call.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/lib/debug.ts plus a focused lib debug test.

items.title: Top-level rustdoc incorrectly says the 80-writer stress test is ignored
items.recommendation: Update the `crates/anvil-witness/src/lib.rs` deferred follow-up text to match the current test state, or remove the deferred follow-up entirely if MLP2-015 completed it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests exercise writer concurrency behaviour, but they do not validate rustdoc accuracy or cross-document consistency.
items.minimumFixScope: Edit the stale crate-level documentation in `crates/anvil-witness/src/lib.rs`.

items.title: Runtime BMAD enums are exported as types only from the BMAD module index
items.recommendation: Move BMADDocumentType and RequirementType into the value export from ./types.js, and remove them from the type-only export block.

items.title: BMAD parser enforces the 2 MB guard with UTF-16 length instead of UTF-8 bytes
items.recommendation: Change the BMAD guard to use Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') or a shared byte-size helper matching the generic parser.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included byte-limit regression tests exercise parseGeneric only; there is no equivalent BMAD test for multi-byte content over the byte limit.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BMAD parser test mirroring packages/adapters/src/generic/__tests__/parser.test.ts: build emoji content whose UTF-8 byte length exceeds MAX_INPUT_SIZE while content.length does not, and assert parseBMADDocument or adapter.parse rejects it with the maximum-size error.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/parser.ts plus a BMAD-specific parser regression test.

items.title: Structured BMAD path conversion errors are collected and then dropped
items.recommendation: Make path-conversion failures observable: either throw when errors is non-empty so adapter.parse returns createParseError, or change bmadToAPS to return diagnostics and pass them through ParseResult warnings/errors. Warnings such as NO_CHANGES should likewise be surfaced if they are intentionally non-fatal.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The available path-safety test for BMAD uses a malformed requirement id that the requirement regex ignores; it does not exercise invalid paths inside structured BMAD YAML where this errors array is populated.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a structured agent YAML test with metadata.id set to ../agent.md and assert adapter.parse returns success false with an INVALID_PATH error, or success true with a warning if partial conversion is the intended contract.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/parser.ts and packages/adapters/src/bmad/format-adapter.ts diagnostic plumbing, plus structured YAML invalid-path tests.

items.title: Generated plans cannot validate against the exported APS schema
items.recommendation: Either make `createPlan` produce a full `APSPlan` including a valid hash, or rename/type/document it as a draft-plan creator and provide a separate finalisation helper that computes the hash before validation.
items.reproduction: Call `const plan = createPlan({ id: 'aps-12345678', intent: 'create a valid APS plan', provenance: { timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), source: 'manual', version: '0.1.0' } }); validatePlan(plan)`. Validation fails because `hash` is missing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the type signature currently masks the mismatch by returning `Omit<APSPlan, 'hash'>` instead of checking that the helper output validates against `APSPlanSchema`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a contract test that creates a plan via `createPlan`, passes it through the intended final public validation path, and asserts the result is valid or, if drafts are intended, asserts a clearly named draft schema accepts it while `APSPlanSchema` rejects it.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/contracts/schemas/aps.schema.ts

items.title: Quoted non-ASCII git paths are decoded as Latin-1 bytes instead of UTF-8
items.recommendation: Decode quoted octal escapes as bytes and then run them through TextDecoder('utf-8'), or avoid quoted-path parsing by using git porcelain -z output and NUL-safe parsing for all status reads.
items.reproduction: With core.quotePath enabled, a status line like ` M "caf\303\251.ts"\n` is parsed to `cafÃ©.ts`; filtering an input path `/repo/café.ts` then produces no match because the parsed absolute path is `/repo/cafÃ©.ts`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current git-status tests cover quoted spaces and rename arrows, but all quoted path examples are ASCII; none exercise git's octal byte escaping for UTF-8 filenames.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock gitExec to return ` M "caf\303\251.ts"\n`, then assert getFileStatus('/repo/café.ts').path is `café.ts`, filterUnstaged(['/repo/café.ts']) includes the file, and getChangedFiles('/repo') returns `/repo/café.ts`.
items.minimumFixScope: Update git-status quoted path decoding and add focused non-ASCII path coverage in git-status.test.ts.

items.title: require-mock-cleanup accepts commented or stringified restoreAllMocks
items.recommendation: Detect `vi.restoreAllMocks()` by walking CallExpression nodes inside the afterEach callback body, not by matching callback source text. Add invalid cases for comments and string literals containing the same token.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked invalid test covers `vi.clearAllMocks()` without a restore call, but it does not include a comment or string literal containing `vi.restoreAllMocks(` inside the callback.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an invalid RuleTester case where a file calls `vi.mock()` and afterEach contains `// vi.restoreAllMocks()` or `const text = 'vi.restoreAllMocks()'` but no actual restore call.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/rules/require-mock-cleanup.ts` and its rule tests.

items.title: Published plugin metadata reports stale version
items.recommendation: Keep `plugin.meta.version` in sync with `package.json`, preferably by generating it during build or adding a release check that fails on mismatch.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests only exercise rule behavior and do not assert plugin metadata or package manifest consistency.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small test that imports the plugin and package manifest and asserts `plugin.meta.version === packageJson.version`.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/index.ts` and add a metadata consistency test.

items.title: Recommended usage applies test-only rules to every file
items.recommendation: Either export a flat recommended config scoped to test globs such as `**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}` or clearly document that consumers must wrap `anvil.configs.recommended.rules` in their own test-file override. If legacy config support is required, expose separate legacy and flat configs.
items.reproduction: Use the README's eslint.config.mjs snippet, then lint `src/index.ts` containing `const value = input as any;`. The test-only rule is enabled for that non-test file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The RuleTester cases exercise AST snippets without filenames and there is no integration test for the recommended config against test and non-test file paths.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a config-level test that applies the recommended config to both `src/foo.ts` and `src/foo.test.ts`, asserting test-only rules only run for the test path or documenting the expected override behaviour.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/index.ts`, README usage, and add a config integration test.

items.title: require-cwd-restoration does not verify cwd capture and restore order
items.recommendation: Track ordering using node locations or ranges: require the saved cwd capture to occur before the first mutating `process.chdir`, and require the restoring `process.chdir(savedCwd)` to occur after the last mutating chdir. Consider tracking this within beforeEach/afterEach scopes if that is the intended contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover correct save-before-change patterns and missing restoration, but not capture-after-change or restoration-before-final-change false negatives.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add invalid cases for `process.chdir('/tmp'); const originalCwd = process.cwd(); process.chdir(originalCwd);` and `const originalCwd = process.cwd(); process.chdir(originalCwd); process.chdir('/tmp');`.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/rules/require-cwd-restoration.ts` and its rule tests.

items.title: Resolution detection ignores transition order
items.recommendation: Require evidence that success occurs after failure, either by preserving signal order and comparing indexes or by using per-observation timestamps from the group/observations if available. If ObservationGroup.signals is intentionally unordered, the rule should not claim transition semantics without additional ordered evidence.
items.reproduction: Call createResolutionRule().evaluate() with an ObservationGroup whose signals are ['success_signal', 'failure_signal']; the rule returns fired: true because both signals are present.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests cover the positive ordered case and missing-success negative case, but do not cover reversed signal order.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a ResolutionRule test asserting that ['success_signal', 'failure_signal'] does not fire, or that the rule uses timestamped observations to verify failure precedes success.
items.minimumFixScope: Update ResolutionRule.evaluate and its tests; no package export changes are required.

items.title: Send migration union accepts a real-send payload with dryRun:true
items.recommendation: Make the union discriminant exclusive. For example, add an explicit rejecting field to the send branch such as `dryRun: z.never().optional()` or make the send object strict and add tests for mixed dry-run/send payloads. If other response schemas intentionally allow additive fields, scope strictness to this discriminated union only.
items.reproduction: SendMigrationResponseSchema.parse({ dryRun: true, source: 'manual', total: 1, sent: 1, failed: 0, results: [] }) succeeds through SendResponseSchema instead of rejecting the impossible discriminator state.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the schema file has no included regression case asserting that `dryRun: true` is rejected on the real-send branch.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a vitest case for `SendMigrationResponseSchema.safeParse({ dryRun: true, source: 'manual', total: 1, sent: 1, failed: 0, results: [] })` expecting `success` to be false, plus a valid real-send response without `dryRun` expecting success.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `SendResponseSchema` or `SendMigrationResponseSchema` in `packages/shared/admin-contracts/src/index.ts` and add focused schema tests for the send-migration discriminator.

items.title: Admin key creation can race and leave multiple active keys for one actor
items.recommendation: Enforce the invariant at the database boundary with a partial unique index on active actor_email rows, and make the script use an atomic insert/upsert or an advisory transaction lock keyed by actor_email. Treat unique-conflict failures as the existing different-hash case and keep the audit write in the same transaction.
items.reproduction: Run two admin-key-manage.mjs create processes concurrently against the same database with the same ACTOR_EMAIL and different BEARER_HEX values when no active row exists. Both can pass the SELECT at lines 57-62 before either INSERT commits.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included infra tests cover DNS and Vercel resources; none exercise infra/scripts/admin-key-manage.mjs or concurrent admin key provisioning.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test for admin-key-manage.mjs that starts two concurrent creates for the same actor with different bearers and asserts only one active admin_keys row can exist, with the losing operation failing cleanly.
items.minimumFixScope: infra/scripts/admin-key-manage.mjs plus the migration or schema location that defines admin_keys constraints; add a focused admin key provisioning test.

items.title: Vercel ignore command escapes productionBranch but not path arguments
items.recommendation: Apply one consistent path policy before command construction: either validate rootDirectory and every extraWatchPaths entry as safe repo-relative paths, or shell-escape every dynamic argument with a small tested helper. Also reject path traversal and leading dash values so the ignore script cannot receive accidental options.
items.reproduction: Instantiate VercelApp with rootDirectory set to "apps/web; echo injected" or extraWatchPaths containing "docs/foo' ; echo injected #" and inspect the generated ignoreCommand passed to vercel.Project.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests assert productionBranch rejects metacharacters and that ordinary extra watch paths work, but they do not include malicious or malformed rootDirectory and extraWatchPaths values.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add VercelApp tests that reject or safely quote rootDirectory and extraWatchPaths containing semicolons, whitespace, embedded single quotes, path traversal, and leading dashes.
items.minimumFixScope: infra/src/components/vercel-app.ts and infra/src/__tests__/vercel-app.test.ts.

items.title: scan_artifact_json does not catch registry-load panics
items.recommendation: Move the registry load into the same catch_unwind block as scan_artifact_rust, or wrap the whole scan_artifact_json implementation after JSON argument validation so registry panics are converted through panic_to_error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The referenced registry-missing test covers ordinary load errors returned as Result values, but it does not exercise a panic from registry loading or mapping on scan_artifact_json.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Node integration test or Rust-side injectable loader test that forces the scan entrypoint's registry-load path to panic and asserts scanArtifactJson throws a JS Error instead of aborting the process.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-checks-napi/src/lib.rs scan_artifact_json panic boundary

items.title: Public rate limit can be bypassed by spoofing X-Forwarded-For
items.recommendation: Only derive the client key from a trusted platform-provided value after confirming the edge overwrites client-supplied forwarding headers, or combine a trusted IP signal with an authenticated/session key where available. Add tests that demonstrate spoofed forwarding headers cannot bypass the limit under the supported deployment model.
items.reproduction: Configure rateLimiter({ max: 1 }) and send two requests with different X-Forwarded-For values such as 203.0.113.1 and 203.0.113.2. Both requests use separate buckets and avoid the 429.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests cover adminRateLimit only; they do not exercise apps/anvil-api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts or spoofed forwarding headers.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a rateLimiter test that sends repeated requests with varied X-Forwarded-For headers and asserts the configured trust model either normalises them to the same client bucket or rejects untrusted header input.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts plus a focused unit test for the public limiter's client-key derivation.

items.title: Admin authentication has no linked regression coverage
items.recommendation: Add focused adminAuth tests with mocked db/client and db/queries modules. Cover missing/malformed Authorization, shared-key success ignoring X-Admin-Actor, active per-operator success, revoked per-operator rejection and audit metadata, unknown bearer audit behaviour, and DB lookup fallback to the shared key path.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The associated test file is scoped to adminRateLimit and uses a lightweight stand-in for adminAuth rather than mounting or asserting adminAuth itself.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/admin-auth.test.ts that mounts adminAuth in a Hono app and mocks process.env, findAdminKeyByHash, insertAuditLog, and getClient for each auth branch.
items.minimumFixScope: Add admin-auth unit tests; no production code change is required for the test gap itself.

items.title: Node-only timer unref conflicts with the wrangler dev runtime
items.recommendation: Guard the unref call, for example by assigning the timer to a variable and calling unref only when typeof timer === 'object' and typeof timer.unref === 'function'. Alternatively, align the dev command and supported runtime so this code only runs under Node.
items.reproduction: Run the app in an environment where global setInterval returns a numeric timer id, then call rateLimiter() or adminRateLimit(...). The chained .unref() call attempts to invoke a missing method and throws a TypeError.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked Vitest tests run under Node semantics, where setInterval returns a Timeout with unref, and they do not simulate the wrangler timer API.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Stub global.setInterval to return a numeric id and assert that both rateLimiter() and adminRateLimit(...) construct without throwing.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts and apps/anvil-api/src/middleware/admin-rate-limit.ts timer setup.

items.title: Generic package generator emits the wrong npm scope
items.recommendation: Change the generic package generator to derive @eddacraft-owned package names consistently with the repo convention for each supported directory, and add explicit assertions for generated package.json name values.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and the generated package manifest contract is not asserted in the included files.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a generator unit test that runs the package generator for representative directories such as packages/anvil and packages/shared, then asserts the emitted package.json name uses the expected @eddacraft namespace.
items.minimumFixScope: tools/generators/src/generators/package/generator.ts plus generator tests for package name derivation

items.title: Generator options are used as paths and TypeScript source without validation or escaping
items.recommendation: Validate generator names as safe path segments before constructing paths, reject dot segments and path separators, validate directories at runtime for programmatic callers, and escape generated TypeScript literals with JSON.stringify or a small template helper. Sanitize or escape comment text separately.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and the generated output is not tested with malformed names or descriptions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add generator tests that pass names containing ../, /, quotes, and leading digits plus descriptions containing quotes/comment terminators, asserting the generator rejects unsafe input or emits escaped valid TypeScript without writing outside the target root.
items.minimumFixScope: Input normalisation/validation and template escaping in tools/generators/src/generators/gate-check/generator.ts and tools/generators/src/generators/package/generator.ts; optionally apply the same escaping helper to tools/generators/src/generators/anvil-package/generator.ts descriptions

items.title: Concurrent locks for different tasks can overwrite state.json
items.recommendation: Serialise all state.json mutations with a repository-level state lock, or implement an atomic compare-and-retry loop that rereads and merges on conflict before rename. Keep the per-task lock for first-lock-wins semantics, but do not rely on it to protect shared state writes.
items.reproduction: Create a plan with TEST-001 and TEST-002, start two TaskLocker instances concurrently, call lock('TEST-001') and lock('TEST-002') with Promise.all, then read .anvil/state.json. Depending on interleaving, only one task entry can remain even though both lock calls succeeded and both execution files exist.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover concurrent acquisition for the same task and raw lock-file behaviour for different tasks, but they do not run TaskLocker.lock concurrently for different task IDs and assert that both state records are preserved.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a TaskLocker test that concurrently locks TEST-001 and TEST-002, expects both operations to succeed, and then asserts readStateFile(tempDir).tasks contains both task IDs with locked status.
items.minimumFixScope: State file mutation path in packages/aps/src/state/index.ts plus a concurrency regression test in packages/aps/src/state/state.test.ts.

items.title: Index detection accepts heading variants that parseIndex then ignores
items.recommendation: Share one section-normalisation helper between loader, validator, and parseIndex, or update parseIndex to use the same `normalizedText === 'modules' || normalizedText.startsWith('modules')` predicate when selecting the modules section.
items.reproduction: Use an APS index with `## Modules & Scopes`, a `### auth` module, and a Path list item. loadPlan detects it as an index, calls parseIndex, and returns a multi-module plan with modules.size === 0.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The loader test mentions case-insensitive detection but loads the existing system-ecommerce fixture; parse-index tests only use `## Modules` and do not cover heading variants accepted by detectIndexFile.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add parseIndex/loadPlan coverage for an index headed `## Modules & Scopes` and assert the module metadata is parsed and loaded.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/parser/parse-index.ts and a parser or loader regression test.

items.title: Generated task templates use Markdown links that the task parser stores as labels instead of URLs
items.recommendation: Teach field extraction to preserve link URLs for the Link field, either by passing AST nodes through field assignment or by making extractFieldsFromParagraph append `link.url` when the active key is Link. Add coverage for the template form.
items.reproduction: Parse a task containing `**Link:** [PROJ-123](https://jira.example.com/browse/PROJ-123)`. The resulting task.link is `PROJ-123` rather than `https://jira.example.com/browse/PROJ-123`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The parser test covers only a plain URL value and the generator tests only check that the Link placeholder exists; no test parses a generated/template-style Markdown link.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parseTaskFields or parseDocument test with `**Link:** [PROJ-123](https://jira.example.com/browse/PROJ-123)` and assert task.link is the URL.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/parser/parse-task.ts plus parser tests.

items.title: Release publish target points at dist without a manifest-producing build step
items.recommendation: Add an explicit packaging step that copies or generates package.json and required metadata into dist before nx-release-publish, or change packageRoot to the project root if publishing should use the root manifest with dist entrypoints.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise source behaviour under Vitest. There is no packaging test or dry-run publish check that verifies dist contains a valid package manifest after the build target.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package build verification that runs the build target in CI and asserts packages/aps/dist/package.json exists with the expected name, exports, main, types, and files needed for publish.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/package.json/project.json release target or an added package preparation script.

items.title: Storage interface leaks Buffer without declaring a Node type dependency
items.recommendation: Either avoid Buffer in the public port by using Uint8Array or an explicit project-owned binary type, or import the Buffer type from node:buffer and declare the necessary Node type dependency for consumers.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and normal in-repo typechecking can pass because the workspace compiler configuration supplies Node globals.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a declaration-consumer smoke test with a minimal tsconfig that imports IStorageProvider from @eddacraft/anvil-ports without inheriting the monorepo's ambient Node types.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/ports/src/interfaces/storage.interface.ts and packages/anvil/ports/package.json if Buffer remains part of the public API.

items.title: Ports public API depends on core despite the contracts-only package contract
items.recommendation: Change the type import in check.interface.ts to @eddacraft/anvil-contracts, update the package dependency to @eddacraft/anvil-contracts, and align any TypeScript project references with the same boundary.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this source group, and there is no package-boundary or declaration-surface test asserting that @eddacraft/anvil-ports declarations avoid @eddacraft/anvil-core.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package boundary test or declaration smoke test that builds @eddacraft/anvil-ports and asserts dist/**/*.d.ts and package.json do not reference @eddacraft/anvil-core while still resolving APSPlan and WarningResult from @eddacraft/anvil-contracts.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/ports/src/interfaces/check.interface.ts and packages/anvil/ports/package.json, plus the ports TypeScript references if they currently point at core.

items.title: Website production build can ship TypeScript errors
items.recommendation: Either remove typescript.ignoreBuildErrors or make the website build path explicitly depend on the website typecheck target, including the command used by Vercel/package builds. Keep the README and AGENTS command guidance aligned with the enforced build path.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or configuration checks assert that the website production build fails on TypeScript errors or that nx build website depends on website:typecheck.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small configuration test that fails when apps/website/next.config.mjs enables ignoreBuildErrors without a website build target or package build script that runs typechecking first.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/website/next.config.mjs plus the website build wiring in apps/website/package.json and/or apps/website/project.json

items.title: Public export map and root barrel expose different runtime surfaces
items.recommendation: Make the public API consistent: either add ./concurrency to package.json exports and export feature-flags from src/index.ts, or deliberately document and test the asymmetry. Prefer adding the missing concurrency subpath because all other module barrels are exported as subpaths, and add a root feature-flags re-export if the root entrypoint is meant to aggregate public runtime APIs.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests import modules via relative paths such as ./git-agent.js and provider files, so they bypass package.json exports and the root barrel entirely.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package API smoke test that imports from @eddacraft/anvil-runtime, @eddacraft/anvil-runtime/cache, @eddacraft/anvil-runtime/watch, @eddacraft/anvil-runtime/feature-flags, and @eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency after build, asserting expected representative exports exist.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/package.json, packages/anvil/runtime/src/index.ts, and one package-level export smoke test

items.title: Generated OpenAPI artifact is excluded from the published package file list
items.recommendation: Add openapi.json to package.json files, or move/copy the generated artifact under an included directory such as dist during build/release. If the spec is intentionally repo-local only, document that and keep it out of release expectations.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or packaging checks were provided, and the package scripts do not include a pack/dry-run assertion that openapi.json is present in the package contents.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package dry-run test or release check that runs generate:openapi and verifies the packed file list contains packages/kindling-integration/openapi.json when the artifact is expected to ship.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/kindling-integration/package.json and, if needed, the generator output path or release script.

items.title: Text output format is advertised without a text response contract
items.recommendation: Either remove text from the format enum until the API is JSON-only, or add explicit text/plain response content for each operation with the correct schema/description for text output.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for the generator or generated OpenAPI document, and the package test script does not show any assertion that parameter formats and response media types stay consistent.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Generate the OpenAPI document and assert that every operation accepting format=text declares a text/plain 200 response, or assert that JSON-only operations do not include text in the format enum.
items.minimumFixScope: Update commonQueryParams and/or each operation's 200 response content in packages/kindling-integration/scripts/generate-openapi.ts.

items.title: Explicit undefined severity default is documented but not honoured
items.recommendation: Either preserve the documented contract by distinguishing omitted arguments from an explicit second argument, or remove the undefined-default overload/example and make the always-default-to-info contract explicit.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included severity test checks explicit undefined only with valid values, not invalid strings or non-string inputs where the default path is used.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add expectations for parseSeverity('invalid', undefined) and parseSeverity(123, undefined) matching the intended contract.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/utils/severity.ts and packages/anvil/core/src/utils/severity.test.ts

items.title: Relative path validation accepts internal parent-directory segments despite its contract
items.recommendation: If the documented contract is intended, inspect path segments before normalisation and reject any segment equal to '..'. If normalising internal '..' is intended, update the comments and add tests that codify this narrower guarantee.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No path-safety tests are included for validateRelativePath, and the linked tests only cover git operations and severity parsing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add validateRelativePath cases for '../x', 'x/../../y', and 'x/../y', asserting the intended accept/reject behaviour explicitly.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/utils/path-safety.ts and a focused path-safety test file

items.title: Structured debug data bypasses log sanitisation
items.recommendation: Sanitise structured data before logging, for example with a small recursive serializer/replacer that applies sanitizeForLog to string leaves and redacts known secret-bearing keys, or restrict the API to string/Error data and document that constraint.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included tests exercise debug.ts or structured data sanitisation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add debug tests that enable ANVIL_DEBUG, log an object containing sk-/Bearer-like values, and assert console.debug does not receive raw secret strings.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/utils/debug.ts plus a debug utility test file

items.title: APS drift check crashes on malformed release records despite being advisory
items.recommendation: Wrap release-record loading in try/catch and add a warning finding such as release-record-unreadable or release-record-invalid-json, leaving releaseRecord null so the rest of the advisory checks can still run.
items.reproduction: Run `node scripts/aps/drift-check.mjs --release-record /tmp/bad.json --json` where /tmp/bad.json contains `{`. The process throws a SyntaxError instead of returning advisory JSON with a warning finding.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied, and the release-record path has no visible malformed-input handling.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend scripts/aps/_test/drift-check.test.sh with a malformed release-record fixture and assert --json exits 0 with an advisory finding instead of throwing.
items.minimumFixScope: scripts/aps/drift-check.mjs release-record parsing and drift-check tests

items.title: docs-check can erase a baseline surface when regeneration fails
items.recommendation: Load the existing baseline before regeneration, replace only surfaces that successfully produce parseable JSON, and exit non-zero without writing when any baselineable surface fails unexpectedly.
items.reproduction: Seed docs/governance/docs-check.baseline.json with a links entry, make scripts/docs/check-links.mjs emit no JSON or invalid JSON under --json, then run pnpm docs:check:update-baseline. The rewritten baseline omits the links entry instead of preserving it or failing without writing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied, and the owned code has no visible guard or assertion for failed baseline regeneration preserving existing entries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs-check baseline test that seeds metadata/tags/links entries, forces one baselineable surface to emit no JSON or invalid JSON, runs --update-baseline, and asserts the old entry is preserved or the command fails without rewriting the file.
items.minimumFixScope: scripts/docs/docs-check.mjs regenerateBaseline plus docs-check baseline-regeneration tests

items.title: Malformed percent escapes crash the link checker
items.recommendation: Decode href components through a helper that catches URIError and returns a structured error message for that link. Keep scanning the remaining links in the file.
items.reproduction: Add a governed Markdown link such as `[bad](./target.md#bad%zz)` and run `node scripts/docs/check-links.mjs --json`. The checker throws rather than reporting a structured links finding for the offending file and line.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied, and the current control flow has no error handling around per-link decode failures.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a check-links test fixture with a malformed percent escape in a path and anchor, then assert the checker reports ERROR findings with file and line instead of crashing.
items.minimumFixScope: scripts/docs/check-links.mjs resolveLink decode handling and link-check tests

items.title: docs-check silently ignores unknown command-line flags
items.recommendation: Use node:util parseArgs for docs-check too, declare --update-baseline and --no-baseline, and reject unknown options with exit code 2.
items.reproduction: Run `node scripts/docs/docs-check.mjs --no-basline`. The misspelled flag is ignored and the command runs with the baseline enabled.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied, and the current parser has no branch that can reject unknown arguments.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs-check CLI test that invokes `node scripts/docs/docs-check.mjs --not-a-real-flag` and asserts exit code 2 plus an error message.
items.minimumFixScope: scripts/docs/docs-check.mjs argument parsing and docs-check CLI tests

items.title: Generator templates interpolate unescaped user strings into TypeScript
items.recommendation: Centralise template rendering helpers: validate/sanitise names into safe kebab-case and PascalCase identifiers, reject unsupported input early, and render TypeScript string literals with `JSON.stringify` or an equivalent escaping helper. Avoid putting raw descriptions inside block comments unless comment terminators are escaped or removed.
items.reproduction: Run the gate-check generator with name `policy.check` or description `owner's approval`; the emitted check source will not parse as TypeScript.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied for this package, and the generated placeholder tests only assert `true` or basic fields after generation; they do not exercise special characters or invalid identifiers.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add Vitest tests using an Nx in-memory Tree for gate-check, package, and anvil-package generators with apostrophes, newlines, `*/`, and invalid identifier characters, asserting either valid escaped TypeScript output or a clear validation error.
items.minimumFixScope: Update generator input normalisation, template literal rendering, and schema validation for the affected generators, plus focused Tree-based regression tests.

items.title: Build script does not produce a self-contained generator package
items.recommendation: Make the package artifact explicit: either package from the source root with a `files`/pack configuration that includes `generators.json`, schemas, and compiled JS paths, or add a build step that copies generator manifests and schema JSON into `dist` and points package metadata at the built locations. Add a pack/load validation step before release.
items.reproduction: Build the package and inspect the output artifact rooted at `tools/generators/dist`; it will contain compiled TypeScript output but not the root generator collection metadata required by the package manifest.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or package smoke checks were supplied, and the package manifest has no test script that verifies built or packed generator discovery.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a build/pack smoke test that runs the generator package build, inspects `npm pack --dry-run` contents, and loads the generator collection from the produced artifact.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust `tools/generators/package.json` build/pack metadata and asset-copy handling for generator manifests and schema files.

items.title: Typecheck script writes build artefacts into the source tree
items.recommendation: Make the intent explicit by changing the script to `tsc --noEmit` or adding `"noEmit": true` to `apps/docs-public/tsconfig.json`.
items.reproduction: Run the package typecheck in a clean worktree and inspect `apps/docs-public` for emitted `.js` or declaration files if `@docusaurus/tsconfig` does not set `noEmit`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests or validation fixtures were provided for this package's project scripts or TypeScript compiler behaviour.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a lightweight script/CI check that runs the docs-public typecheck and asserts the worktree remains clean, or include this package in an existing build hygiene check.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the docs-public TypeScript typecheck configuration or script only.

items.title: Published package does not export its documented concurrency subpath
items.recommendation: Add './concurrency' to package.json exports with dist/concurrency/index.js and dist/concurrency/index.d.ts, or change all documented/generated usage to import concurrency APIs from the root export.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests import source files relatively and do not build the package then test public package subpath resolution through the package exports map.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: After building the package, run a Node ESM import of '@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency' from a package-consumer context and assert prepareCommitMsgHook is available.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/package.json and a package-exports smoke test

items.title: Queue file updates are only serialised for join, so leave and cleanup can lose entries
items.recommendation: Centralise queue mutation behind a helper that acquires `${queuePath}.lock`, and use it for join, leave, cleanupTimedOut, and cleanupAllTimedOut writes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The queue tests exercise join, leave, status, and priority ordering sequentially. They do not interleave leave or cleanup with another process joining the same queue.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Use two QueueManager instances for different agents, arrange a slow leave or cleanup interleaved with another join on the same resource, then assert the final queue contains exactly the expected remaining entries.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/concurrency/queue-manager.ts plus concurrent queue mutation tests in packages/anvil/runtime/src/concurrency/queue-manager.test.ts

items.title: Expired lock takeover can grant the same lock to multiple agents
items.recommendation: Protect forceAcquire with the same per-lock sentinel used by createLock, or implement a compare-and-swap check that re-reads the lock immediately before writing and fails if the observed holder/version changed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included stale-lock test covers a single agent taking over an expired lock sequentially; it does not run two takeover attempts concurrently or assert that only one caller receives acquired: true.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create an expired lock, start two LockManager instances with different agents, call acquire for the same resource concurrently, and assert exactly one result is acquired while the other reports the new holder.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/concurrency/lock-manager.ts plus a concurrent stale/expired takeover regression in packages/anvil/runtime/src/concurrency/lock-manager.test.ts

items.title: Symlink escape checks are time-of-check/time-of-use races
items.recommendation: For security-sensitive callers, avoid operating on mutable attacker-controlled directory trees. Implement path traversal using file-descriptor-relative traversal where available, opening each path segment with no-follow semantics and performing the final read/write/delete relative to the validated directory handle. If Node portability prevents this, document that FileStorage only protects against non-racing traversal and symlink state, and require baseDir contents not be concurrently attacker-writable.
items.reproduction: Create baseDir/safe/file.txt, call storage.write('safe/file.txt', ...), and between resolvePath returning and fs.writeFile executing replace baseDir/safe with a symlink to an outside directory. The write can follow the new symlink because the final operation uses the original string path rather than a directory handle or no-follow/openat-style traversal.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing symlink tests create symlinks before the storage call and verify the static check path. They do not exercise a concurrent directory replacement between resolvePath and the final fs operation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with an injected filesystem adapter or a test seam around resolvePath/final fs operation that swaps an intermediate directory to an outside symlink after validation and asserts the final operation does not escape baseDir.
items.minimumFixScope: FileStorage path resolution and filesystem operation implementation; likely requires changing resolvePath from returning a validated string to performing operations through validated directory handles or explicitly documenting the narrower security contract.

items.title: Template defaults leak mutable nested state across calls
items.recommendation: Return a deep clone of the template layer record, including each layer object and its arrays, or freeze the template constants and clone on output.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The template test only asserts the returned top-level object is a different reference; it does not mutate nested layer fields or verify subsequent calls are isolated.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mutate getTemplateDefaults('layered').presentation.depends_on and then call getTemplateDefaults('layered') again; the second result should not contain the mutation. Repeat via createDefinitionFromTemplate.
items.minimumFixScope: Change getTemplateDefaults to deep-clone LayersRecord and cover nested mutation isolation.

items.title: Explicit Rego rule predicates interpolate unescaped layer names
items.recommendation: Emit Rego string literals with JSON.stringify or a single shared string-literal escaping helper for rule.from, rule.to, rule.name-derived output, and messages.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The generator tests use simple identifier-like layer and rule names, so they verify structure but not escaping for custom names.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Generate a policy for layers whose names contain quotes or newlines and assert the output passes Rego parsing or at least contains correctly escaped string literals.
items.minimumFixScope: Update explicit-rule string emission in rego-generator.ts and add escaping tests for custom layer/rule names.

items.title: Baseline violation IDs can collide for distinct paths
items.recommendation: Use a collision-resistant ID, for example a sha256 hash over a structured tuple of fromFile, toFile, and line, or encode each component reversibly before joining. Consider a compatibility path for existing baseline IDs during migration.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included baseline and edge-detector tests verify deterministic IDs and simple different inputs, but they do not include two distinct paths that sanitise to the same string.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert createViolationId('src/a-b.ts','src/c.ts',1) differs from createViolationId('src/a_b.ts','src/c.ts',1), and assert baseline classification does not mark the second edge as existing when only the first is baselined.
items.minimumFixScope: Update createViolationId and all baseline comparison call sites that rely on its format; add collision regression coverage.

items.title: Sensitive observations can still be persisted unredacted
items.recommendation: Route AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit through the same observation validation and sensitive-data enforcement as KindlingService, and make redaction fail closed: after redaction, re-run sensitive validation and reject or throw if sensitive markers remain. Add coverage for adapter emission and for detected-but-not-redacted token forms.
items.reproduction: Pass an action_executed observation with details.command set to `deploy --token abc123` through AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit, or through KindlingService.emit with a recording store; the serialized stored observation still contains `abc123`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included malicious-ai tests verify containsSensitiveData detects several strings and that schemas reject bad query shapes, but they do not assert what KindlingService or AnvilKindlingAdapter actually persists after detection/redaction.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests with a fake appendObservation/store that emit an observation containing `--token abc123` through both KindlingService.emit and AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit, then assert the stored content does not include the token or that emission is rejected.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/kindling-integration/src/adapter.ts, packages/kindling-integration/src/sensitive-data-validator.ts, and targeted tests under packages/kindling-integration/src/.

items.title: Convenience query methods do not enforce caller-supplied limits after store over-return
items.recommendation: Carry the effective request limits into the post-query enforcement step, for example by applying enforceQueryLimits(response, { max_results: request.max_results, max_payload_bytes: request.max_payload_bytes }) in each convenience method after service.query returns.
items.reproduction: Use a fake store whose query method returns 50 valid observations regardless of request.max_results, configure query_limits.max_results to 100, then call KindlingQueryService.querySession(id, { max_results: 10 }); the returned response contains 50 observations instead of 10.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests validate schema maximums and truncation metadata shape, but they do not exercise KindlingQueryService against a store that returns more rows or bytes than requested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a KindlingQueryService test with a fake KindlingService/store returning more observations than requested and assert querySession/queryPlan/queryGate/queryAction truncate to the per-call max_results and update metadata.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/kindling-integration/src/query-service.ts plus focused query-service tests.

items.title: Warning result consistency validation ignores most summary fields
items.recommendation: Recompute and compare every summary aggregate: total, all expected severity counts, category counts, suppressed count, and blocking count. Treat missing expected severity/category entries according to the intended summary contract.
items.reproduction: A WarningResult with one unsuppressed error warning, summary.total = 1, summary.bySeverity = { error: 1 }, summary.blocking = 0, and summary.suppressed = 99 passes validateWarningResultConsistency even though the summary is wrong.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise warning.schema.ts helpers or malformed WarningResult summaries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that validateWarningResultConsistency returns false when byCategory, suppressed, blocking, or an expected bySeverity count is missing or wrong.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/warning.schema.ts plus a focused warning schema test file.

items.title: Targeting rules can reference variants that do not exist
items.recommendation: In FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.check, validate each targeting rule's variant against the variant key set and add an issue at ['targeting', index, 'variant'] when it is missing.
items.reproduction: FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.safeParse(validFlag({ targeting: [{ conditions: [{ attribute: 'environment', operator: 'equals', value: 'prod' }], variant: 'missing' }] })).success is true.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The targeting tests only cover valid targeting rules and optional targeting; they do not include a rule whose variant is absent from the flag variants.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a feature flag schema test that rejects targeting: [{ conditions: [...], variant: 'nonexistent' }] when variants only contain enabled/disabled.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.ts plus the feature-flags schema test file.

items.title: Percentage targeting accepts values outside 0 to 100
items.recommendation: Add a numeric range check for the percentage operator, accepting only values between 0 and 100 inclusive.
items.reproduction: TargetingConditionSchema.safeParse({ attribute: 'rollout', operator: 'percentage', value: 250 }).success is true, and the same is true for value: -1.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing tests verify that a numeric percentage such as 25 is accepted and a string percentage is rejected, but they do not test negative or above-100 numbers.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests rejecting percentage conditions with value -1 and 101 while accepting 0, 25, and 100.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.ts and packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.test.ts.

items.title: Pool cap behaviour is not covered by the library test
items.recommendation: Add a regression test that validates the cap in an isolated process before any other rayon consumer can initialise the global pool. If direct global-pool testing is too fragile for unit tests, factor the cap calculation into a small pure helper and test that helper, then add one integration or subprocess smoke test for `init_global` applying it first.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The sole included test only calls `init_global()` twice and asserts no panic by implication; its own comment states that it does not assert the resulting thread count.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Run a subprocess or dedicated integration binary that calls `eddacraft_anvil_rayon_init::init_global()` before any `par_iter`, then asserts `rayon::current_num_threads() == (num_cpus::get() / 2).max(1)`.
items.minimumFixScope: Add focused coverage for the cap calculation and first-initialisation behaviour in `crates/anvil-rayon-init`.

items.title: Non-recursive loading silently overwrites duplicate module IDs
items.recommendation: Move the duplicate-ID check so it runs before the recursive/non-recursive split, or add the same `modules.has(moduleId)` ParseError guard to the non-recursive branch.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing `recursive=false` test verifies that content is not loaded, but it uses unique module IDs and does not assert duplicate handling parity with recursive loading.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an index fixture with two modules using the same H3 module ID and assert `loadPlan(path, { recursive: false })` rejects with `ParseError` instead of returning a map with one overwritten entry.
items.minimumFixScope: One duplicate-ID guard in `loadMultiModulePlan` and a focused loader test for `recursive: false`.

items.title: Top-level false-positive module headings load as empty indexes
items.recommendation: Apply the same parseIndex probe at the top level before choosing `loadMultiModulePlan`, and only treat the file as an index when parsed modules are present. Alternatively, narrow `detectIndexFile` to headings the index parser actually supports and make empty indexes fail explicitly.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The false-positive test loads an index fixture whose child module has the `Modules impacted` heading, so it exercises only the nested guard. There is no test for a root leaf spec with a `## Modules impacted` heading.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create a temporary top-level leaf APS document with `## Modules impacted` plus a normal `## Tasks` section, call `loadPlan`, and assert `isMultiModule` is false and the task is present.
items.minimumFixScope: Root detection path in `loadPlan`, plus one loader regression test.

items.title: Public templates entrypoint is not covered by tests
items.recommendation: Add a test that imports the template API through packages/aps/src/templates/index.ts, and ideally an integration/build test that resolves @eddacraft/anvil-aps/templates from the built package exports.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: All current generator tests bypass index.ts and package.json exports by importing ./generator.js directly.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test importing generateAllTemplates and one direct generator function from './index.js' and asserting they produce the same non-empty template output as the direct generator import; add a build/export smoke test for the ./templates subpath if package export tests exist.
items.minimumFixScope: Test-only change covering the templates barrel and exported subpath.

items.title: Trace file creation can follow a raced symlink before validation
items.recommendation: Open trace files with no-follow semantics on Unix, for example OpenOptionsExt::custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW) plus create_new(true) for the absent-file path or an openat-style flow. Keep the post-open inode check, but make the open itself refuse symlinks.
items.reproduction: On Unix, set ANVIL_TRACE_SINK=file=<path in attacker-writable directory>. Race creation of <path> as a symlink after validate_existing_trace_file observes NotFound but before OpenOptions::open runs. The function can open the symlink target before returning TraceSink.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Unix tests cover existing non-regular paths and private regular files, but they do not exercise the missing-path creation case or a symlink substitution race.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Unix test for a missing path where the final path is a symlink at open time, and assert open_trace_file returns an error without creating or opening the symlink target. If deterministic race injection is hard, factor the open path to make the NotFound-to-open transition testable.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-observability/src/lib.rs open_trace_file Unix opening flags and corresponding Unix tests.

items.title: CLI reports success after transform errors
items.recommendation: When `totalErrors > 0`, set `process.exitCode = 1` or throw after printing the summary, and avoid the success message. Consider separating partial-success wording from clean success.
items.reproduction: Trigger any `rewriteImportsInFile` per-import error while another import in the run changes successfully; the command records the error count but still reaches the success message and exits normally.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked CLI tests assert exit status or output when transform errors are present.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CLI-level test or command action unit test that injects a transform result with errors and asserts a non-zero exit code and no success message.
items.minimumFixScope: `tools/codemods/src/cli.ts` error-summary and exit handling.

items.title: Bare core imports are rewritten before symbol splitting can run
