items.recommendation: Handle bare `@eddacraft/anvil-core` imports with symbol-aware splitting before applying direct path rewrites, or exclude the bare core specifier from the simple rewrite path when named imports are present.
items.reproduction: Run the transform on a source file containing `import { APSPlanSchema, GateRunner, OPAExecutor } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core';` with `dryRun: false`; the import remains a single declaration from `@eddacraft/anvil-contracts` instead of being split across contracts, runtime, and policy.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and no included test exercises mixed-symbol bare core imports or compares dry-run output with applied output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Vitest case for `rewriteImportsInFile` with mixed symbols from `@eddacraft/anvil-core`, asserting the saved source contains separate imports from `@eddacraft/anvil-contracts`, `@eddacraft/anvil-runtime`, and `@eddacraft/anvil-policy` with no duplicate/conflicting dry-run changes.
items.minimumFixScope: `tools/codemods/src/transforms/rewrite-imports.ts`, with a focused regression test for bare core split ordering.

items.title: Published package version and CLI version disagree
items.recommendation: Source the CLI version from package metadata at build/runtime, or update the hard-coded version during release in the same change as `package.json`.
items.reproduction: Build or run the CLI and execute `anvil-codemod --version`; it reports `0.0.1` despite the package being versioned `0.3.0-beta`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests cover CLI metadata output, and the package has no visible test entry for the codemod CLI.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CLI metadata test asserting `--version` equals `tools/codemods/package.json` version.
items.minimumFixScope: `tools/codemods/src/cli.ts` version initialisation, optionally with a small metadata test.

items.title: Archived core imports are silently ignored instead of surfaced for review
items.recommendation: Distinguish archived/no-replacement imports from ordinary no-op imports, for example by returning a structured mapping result or by adding an error/manualReview entry when an `@eddacraft/anvil-core/*` path is intentionally unmapped.
items.reproduction: Run the import codemod on a file containing `import { detectDrift } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core/drift';`; the archived import is neither rewritten nor reported as an error/manual-review item.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests cover archived subpaths or assert that intentionally unmapped imports are reported to users.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that imports from each `ARCHIVED_CORE_SUBDIRS` prefix and asserts `rewriteImportsInFile` records an error or manual-review result instead of returning no changes and no errors.
items.minimumFixScope: `tools/codemods/src/import-mappings.ts` and `tools/codemods/src/transforms/rewrite-imports.ts` result handling for intentionally unmapped core imports.

items.title: Provenance schemas accept chains whose observation sessions are not declared
items.recommendation: Add schema-level constraints: source_sessions/session_ids should be non-empty, and ProvenanceChainSchema should refine that every kindling_sources[].session_id is included in source_sessions. Apply the same non-empty session rule to ProvenanceSummarySchema if summaries are expected to preserve session lineage.
items.reproduction: Create a memory whose provenance has one kindling_sources entry with session_id A and source_sessions: []. MemoryObjectSchema.safeParse accepts it, while validateProvenanceIntegrity reports the missing session.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing provenance tests check that validateProvenanceIntegrity can report a missing session, but they do not assert that ProvenanceChainSchema, ProvenanceSummarySchema, or MemoryObjectSchema reject such inconsistent provenance at parse time.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add provenance tests that expect ProvenanceChainSchema.safeParse and MemoryObjectSchema.safeParse to fail when kindling_sources references a session not present in source_sessions, including the empty source_sessions case.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/provenance.ts plus focused provenance and memory schema tests

items.title: Extended memory contract drifts from the base EDDA-001 memory shape
items.recommendation: Define MemoryObjectExtended by extending the inferred MemoryObject type or by reusing the exact base field contracts, especially schema_version and Attribution. Put promotion-specific attribution fields under a separate extension field if they are still needed.
items.reproduction: A TypeScript assignment from MemoryObjectExtended to MemoryObject fails because attribution lacks actor, timestamp, and method, and schema_version is absent.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The associated contract tests cover MemoryObjectSchema but do not import or type-check edda-extended.ts, so this drift is invisible to the current test suite.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a compile-time contract test that constructs a MemoryObjectExtended and asserts it satisfies MemoryObject for the inherited base fields, or refactor MemoryObjectExtended to extend MemoryObject directly so TypeScript enforces the relationship.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/edda-extended.ts and a focused type-level contract test

items.title: Evolution graph validation ignores disagreement between node fields and link edges
items.recommendation: During validation, derive expected edges from node.supersedes and node.superseded_by, compare them with links, and report mismatches in either direction. Alternatively make links the only source of truth and remove relationship fields from EvolutionNode.
items.reproduction: Pass a graph with two nodes whose supersedes arrays are empty and one link from ID_1 to ID_2. validateEvolutionGraph reports valid because there is no cycle and no orphan, even though the node relationship fields deny the link.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Evolution tests cover consistent graphs, cycles, and orphan nodes, but do not include a graph where node supersession fields and link edges disagree.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a validateEvolutionGraph test that builds a graph with link ID_1->ID_2 but ID_2.supersedes missing ID_1, and assert validation returns an issue describing the mismatch.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/evolution.ts plus one focused evolution validation test

items.title: Sensitive observations can still be stored in clear text
items.recommendation: Make one sanitisation path mandatory before any append or emit. Have the adapter validate and redact Anvil observations before serialising them, and update redactSensitiveFields so every detection source has a corresponding redaction rule or so emission fails closed when detected data cannot be redacted. Re-run sensitive validation after redaction before storing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: malicious-ai.test checks containsSensitiveData detection, but it never instantiates KindlingService or AnvilKindlingAdapter with a capture store and asserts the stored observation content is redacted.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests with a fake store/core service that emit observations containing ~/.ssh/private_key and token-bearing error messages through both KindlingService.emit and AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit, then assert no persisted string contains the original secret-bearing value.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/kindling-integration/src/adapter.ts and packages/kindling-integration/src/sensitive-data-validator.ts, with service/adapter persistence tests in packages/kindling-integration/src/malicious-ai.test.ts or a focused companion test.

items.title: Validated observations are persisted without schema normalisation
items.recommendation: Use validation.data as the canonical observation after validation, then run sensitive-data checks and redaction against that normalised value. If unknown observation fields should be rejected rather than stripped, make the observation schemas strict and add explicit rejection tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests validate schema helpers directly and query stripping behaviour, but they do not assert what KindlingService.emit actually passes to IKindlingStore after validation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fake IKindlingStore, emit a session_start observation with an extra top-level field, and assert the stored observation either rejects the input or omits the extra field according to the chosen contract.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/kindling-integration/src/kindling-service.ts plus a focused service emission test.

items.title: Export capability is advertised even though serialization always fails
items.recommendation: Either implement APSPlan-to-APS markdown serialization, or override canExport to return false for APS formats until serialization is implemented. Keep tests aligned with the chosen contract.
items.reproduction: Call adapter.canExport('aps') and then adapter.serialize(validPlan). The first call returns true while the second returns a NOT_IMPLEMENTED serialize error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test only checks canExport returns true and never exercises serialize after capability selection, so the contradictory contract is not detected.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that, for every format where canExport(format) is true, serialize(validPlan) succeeds; or if serialization remains unsupported, assert canExport('aps') and canExport('.aps.md') are false.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/aps-markdown/adapter.ts and its APS markdown adapter tests

items.title: Substring matching misclassifies intents containing non-action words like address as file creation
items.recommendation: Match action keywords on word boundaries or tokenise the title and intent before applying the heuristic. Consider covering common APS verbs such as address, refactor, document, and validate explicitly instead of relying on raw substring checks.
items.reproduction: Parse a task with an intent such as "Address reviewer feedback" and no files. inferChangeType returns file_create because "address" contains "add".
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing inference tests cover positive create/update/delete examples only. They do not include negative cases where an action keyword appears as part of another word.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parse test for an intent like "Address reviewer feedback" and assert it is not classified as file_create, preferably expecting the project’s chosen fallback or update type.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/aps-markdown/adapter.ts and APS markdown adapter inference tests

items.title: Cache key hashing can collide for different input tuples
items.recommendation: Hash a canonical structured representation instead of raw concatenation, for example `JSON.stringify(sortObjectKeys({ plan_hash, config_hash, workspace_root: normaliseWorkspacePath(...), extra }))`, or length-prefix each field before updating the digest.
items.reproduction: Call `generateCacheKey` twice with the same `check_name` and the two input triples `{plan_hash:'ab', config_hash:'c', workspace_root:'d'}` and `{plan_hash:'a', config_hash:'bc', workspace_root:'d'}`; the returned keys are identical.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test changes only one field from `abc123` to `different`, which does not exercise ambiguous variable-length boundaries between adjacent fields.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a `generateCacheKey` test asserting the two boundary-ambiguous inputs above produce different keys.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `generateCacheKey` to encode field boundaries canonically and adjust or add tests for boundary-collision cases.

items.title: Gate config hash depends on object insertion order inside check configs
items.recommendation: Apply the same recursive key sorting used by `hashCheckConfig` to each check config, or to the full `enabledChecks` structure before stringifying.
items.reproduction: Hash checks containing `{ config: { a: 1, b: 2 } }` and `{ config: { b: 2, a: 1 } }`; the current implementation produces different strings because `JSON.stringify` preserves insertion order.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The order-independence test exists only for `hashCheckConfig`; `hashGateConfig` tests do not pass equivalent configs with different key insertion order.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a `hashGateConfig` test asserting equivalent check configs with reversed object key order hash identically.
items.minimumFixScope: Canonicalise `enabledChecks` before `JSON.stringify` in `hashGateConfig` and add the missing order-independence test.

items.title: Email revoke does not prevent new licences from being minted
items.recommendation: Make email revoke invalidate all session-bearing credentials for the user in the same transaction, at minimum refresh_tokens as well as access_tokens. If revoke is meant to remove beta access entirely, also transition the user status or record an explicit revoked entitlement state so non-token login paths cannot regrant the beta fallback.
items.reproduction: Revoke an active user by email, then call POST /api/v1/auth/session/refresh with a previously issued refresh token for that user. The refresh token row is still valid, the user remains active, and with no active access_tokens rows findActiveScopesForUser returns ['beta'], so a new licence is issued.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The admin revoke test only mocks and asserts access token row counts. The refresh tests cover valid, revoked, expired, and reused refresh token rows, but never simulate an admin email revoke that removed access_tokens while leaving refresh_tokens and beta_users active.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration-style route test where /admin/revoke by email is followed by /auth/session/refresh using an existing refresh token; assert refresh fails and refresh_tokens for that user/family are revoked. Add a second test that OTP/device/GitHub issuance does not fall back to beta for a revoked user.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the email branch of /admin/revoke plus the entitlement/session lookup contract used by auth issuance paths.

items.title: OTP active-code cap is raceable under concurrent requests
items.recommendation: Replace count-then-insert with a single atomic operation, such as a transaction using a per-user advisory lock, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the user row, or an INSERT ... SELECT guarded by a locked count. Return the same anti-enumeration success shape when the guarded insert does not happen.
items.reproduction: Start with two active OTP rows for a user and send several concurrent /auth/otp/request calls. Each request can read activeCount=2 before any sibling inserts; all then insert a new row and send an email, producing more than three active codes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests mock countActiveOtpCodes with fixed sequential values and assert behaviour for count 3 and count 2. They do not exercise concurrent requests sharing the same initial count.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a concurrency test around the query helper or route that fires multiple simultaneous OTP requests from an initial count below the cap and asserts no more than MAX_ACTIVE_CODES rows are inserted and no extra emails are sent.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the OTP request persistence helper and update auth-otp.ts to use the atomic insert result.

items.title: Default admin invite returns requested scopes but does not persist them
items.recommendation: Mirror /admin/approve by inserting an access_tokens row with the granted scopes in the default invite transaction, or remove scopes from the default invite contract and response if scoped grants are only supported by tokenOnly/approve.
items.reproduction: Call POST /api/v1/admin/invite with {email, scopes:['preview']} and tokenOnly omitted. The response includes scopes:['preview'], but the default-flow transaction has no INSERT INTO access_tokens; when the invitee polls the confirmed device code, findActiveScopesForUser returns ['beta'].
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The default invite test only uses the default ['beta'] scope and asserts no raw token is returned. It does not request a graded scope or assert that an access_tokens statement is included in the default-flow transaction.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a default /admin/invite test with scopes:['preview','beta'] that asserts the transaction contains INSERT INTO access_tokens with those scopes, then add a device activation test showing the minted JWT includes the requested graded scopes.
items.minimumFixScope: Update /admin/invite default-flow transaction and its tests.

items.title: Refresh rotation can consume the old token before replacement succeeds
items.recommendation: Move refresh rotation into one database transaction that consumes the old row and inserts the replacement atomically, returning the new row only if both operations commit. Consider signing before committing only if failure semantics are explicitly handled, or keep the old token usable until replacement persistence succeeds.
items.reproduction: Make consumeRefreshToken return true and insertRefreshToken throw. The handler exits with an error after the old row has been consumed, and a retry with the same refresh token will hit the consumed-token reuse branch and revoke the family.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The refresh tests cover the happy path, unknown/revoked/expired tokens, reuse, and a lost consume race. They do not cover a failure after consumeRefreshToken succeeds and before insertRefreshToken completes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test where insertRefreshToken rejects after consumeRefreshToken resolves true; assert the implementation does not leave the original token consumed or converts the operation into a transactional failure with no partial state.
items.minimumFixScope: Add a transactional refresh-token rotation helper in db/queries.ts and call it from auth-session.ts.

items.title: Primary renderer API has no render or error-boundary tests
items.recommendation: Add focused React rendering tests for DashboardRenderer using a DOM-capable Vitest environment and the current catalog. Cover at least one minimal valid spec, one invalid spec showing the validation alert, and the wrapper/className behavior; add an error-boundary test if the component can be made injectable or tested through a deliberately throwing catalog entry.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: schema-validator.test.ts and specs.test.ts import validateSpec/getComponentNames only; neither imports DashboardRenderer nor renders React output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create packages/libs/render/src/dashboard-renderer.test.tsx that renders <DashboardRenderer spec={minimalValidSpec} className="sentinel" /> and asserts rendered dashboard text plus the sentinel wrapper, then renders an invalid spec and asserts role="alert" with the validation failure text.
items.minimumFixScope: Add DashboardRenderer-focused tests and, if needed, update vitest.config.ts to use jsdom for that test file or a separate test project.

items.title: Exported warning ID pattern accepts IDs that parser rejects
items.recommendation: Make WARNING_ID_PATTERN encode the same line constraint as parseWarningId, or stop exporting it as a validity contract and document it as a coarse format matcher. A practical fix is to require a positive integer without leading zero-only values, then keep parseWarningId as the final validator.
items.reproduction: WARNING_ID_PATTERN.test('AP-003-file.ts:0') returns true, but isValidWarningId('AP-003-file.ts:0') returns false and parseWarningId('AP-003-file.ts:0') returns null.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: warning-id.test.ts checks invalid zero lines through parseWarningId, but it never asserts WARNING_ID_PATTERN behaviour or consistency with isValidWarningId.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that iterates representative IDs and asserts WARNING_ID_PATTERN.test(id) === isValidWarningId(id), including AP-003-file.ts:0.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/warnings/warning-id.ts and packages/anvil/core/src/warnings/warning-id.test.ts

items.title: Unsupported regex flags can pass validation then fail registry consumers
items.recommendation: Restrict accepted flags to the minimum Node version supported by the package, or encode/runtime-check the minimum engine requirement and ensure scanner consumers reject incompatible compiled registries with a clear error. Add an explicit test for unsupported flags according to the declared support matrix.
items.reproduction: On a Node runtime without `v` flag support, parse a rule containing `detection: { type: regex, pattern: 'x', flags: 'v' }`; schema validation will differ by runtime, and a registry compiled elsewhere can later fail when consumers reconstruct the regex.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The parser tests assert invalid/missing detection fields, but there is no test for regex flag compatibility or for loading a compiled registry on the package's minimum supported Node version.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parser/schema test that a rule with `flags: 'v'` is rejected unless the package declares and enforces a Node version where `v` is supported.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/anvil-format/schemas.ts and the corresponding parse/schema tests.

items.title: UTC TTL calculations use local calendar arithmetic
items.recommendation: Use UTC arithmetic for these helpers: either add/subtract ttlDays * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 from getTime(), or use getUTCDate/setUTCDate consistently. Build lastNDays from the same end timestamp so the range is deterministic.
items.reproduction: Run calculateExpiry for a UTC timestamp crossing a DST boundary under a DST-observing TZ, for example TZ=America/New_York with createdAt='2024-03-09T12:00:00.000Z' and ttlDays=2; local setDate arithmetic can return an expiry one hour off the exact UTC two-day TTL.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included temporal tests validate one fixed winter date and do not set a DST-observing TZ or cover DST boundary dates. lastNDays is only checked for schema validity with 7 days, not for exact UTC duration.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a temporal test that runs expiry/range calculations across a DST transition with a fixed TZ such as America/New_York and asserts the UTC instant differs by exactly N days in milliseconds.
items.minimumFixScope: Update temporal.ts date arithmetic in calculateExpiry and lastNDays, then extend contracts.test.ts temporal utility coverage for DST-boundary UTC calculations.

items.title: Expanded provenance invents invalid ember_source fields
items.recommendation: Do not populate ember_source unless the caller supplies the required proposal_type and confidence, or extend the function signature/options to accept those values. If only proposal_id is available, omit ember_source rather than manufacturing contract-invalid fields.
items.reproduction: Call expandProvenanceSummary with a summary containing proposal_id, then validate the result with ProvenanceChainSchema.safeParse; the ember_source.proposal_type value 'unknown' should fail the schema.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: type-mappings.test.ts asserts that ember_source exists and contains the proposal_id, but does not validate the expanded chain with ProvenanceChainSchema or assert ember_source.proposal_type is a valid ProposalType.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that expands a summary with proposal_id and asserts ProvenanceChainSchema.safeParse(chain).success is true, using supplied proposal_type/confidence or expecting ember_source to be omitted when those fields are unavailable.
items.minimumFixScope: Change expandProvenanceSummary in type-mappings.ts and update type-mappings.test.ts to validate schema compatibility for proposal_id summaries.

items.title: Root package barrel auto-registration is not covered by package tests
items.recommendation: Add a package-level barrel test, for example src/__tests__/index.test.ts, that imports ../index.js and asserts registry.listAdapterNames() contains aps-markdown, bmad, speckit, and generic-markdown in the intended order. Also assert basic detection through the exported registry for representative APS, BMAD, SpecKit, and generic markdown inputs.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests instantiate SpecKitFormatAdapter, BMADFormatAdapter, GenericMarkdownAdapter, and AdapterRegistry directly. They validate the components used by the barrel, but not the public root import side effect or exported registry contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create packages/adapters/src/__tests__/index.test.ts importing { registry } from '../index.js'; assert registry.listAdapterNames() equals ['aps-markdown','bmad','speckit','generic-markdown'] and that registry.detectAdapterWithPath() can select expected adapters for .aps.md, spec.md, and BMAD fixture content.
items.minimumFixScope: Test-only change under packages/adapters/src/__tests__/ for the root entrypoint contract.

items.title: Plain text responses cannot be recovered after JSON parse failure
items.recommendation: Read the response body once with res.text(), then parse JSON from that string when appropriate. For example, inspect the content-type header or try JSON.parse(text) while retaining the original text on parse failure.
items.reproduction: Use createApiClient with an app whose request() returns new Response('ok', { status: 200, headers: { 'content-type': 'text/plain' } }); then await client.get('/plain'). The json() call throws on 'ok', and the catch path attempts res.text() on an already-consumed body.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and createApiClient is not imported by any current apps/e2e/src test file, so there is no direct coverage for non-JSON API responses.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an e2e helper unit test that stubs app.request to return a text/plain Response and asserts client.get() resolves with status 200 and body 'ok'.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/e2e/src/helpers/api-client.ts response body parsing logic plus a focused helper test.

items.title: Task input lists are dropped when another field follows Inputs
items.recommendation: Preserve content order when parsing fields, or associate each list with the immediately preceding field while iterating the original `Array<Paragraph | List>`. Avoid using a global first-list fallback detached from source order.
items.reproduction: Parse a task whose content order is: Intent paragraph, Inputs paragraph, input list, Validation paragraph. `parseTask` filters paragraphs to `[Intent, Inputs, Validation]` and lists to `[inputList]`; `parseTaskFields` sets `lastField` to Validation and never assigns `fields.inputs`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing Inputs tests only cover Inputs as the last field before the list, or direct `parseTaskFields([inputsParagraph], [inputList])` calls. They do not include a field after an Inputs list.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parseTask or parseDocument test where `**Inputs:**` is followed by a bullet list and then `**Validation:**`, asserting both `inputs` and `validation` are populated.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `parseTask`/`parseTaskFields` to process ordered content for list-backed fields, plus add the regression test.

items.title: Empty section checks continue counting headings after the section ends
items.recommendation: In both structure validators, track the active section explicitly and clear it whenever another H2 is reached. Only count H3 entries while the current H2 is exactly the target section.
items.reproduction: Create a leaf APS document with `# Title`, `## Tasks`, then `## Notes` and `### Not a task`; `validateLeafStructure` will set `hasTaskEntries` from the Notes H3 and omit the `"## Tasks" section has no task entries` warning.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The required-section tests cover missing H1, missing `## Tasks`, and missing `## Modules`, but they do not include an empty target section followed by another section containing H3 headings.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add fixtures for an empty `## Tasks` section followed by `## Notes` with an H3, and an empty `## Modules` section followed by another H2/H3; assert the `required-sections` warning is emitted for each target section.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `validateIndexStructure` and `validateLeafStructure` section tracking plus focused validator tests.

items.title: Publish root conflicts with package entrypoint paths
items.recommendation: Choose one publish root and make the manifest match it. Either publish from packages/docs-meta with the existing ./dist entrypoints, or generate/copy a dist/package.json whose main, types, and exports are relative to dist.
items.reproduction: Build the package, place/use the current package manifest under packages/docs-meta/dist as the configured publish root requires, then inspect the packed package: main and exports point at ./dist/... inside the package instead of ./index.js, ./parser/index.js, and ./types/index.js.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise parser behaviour only; they do not build the package, inspect dist contents, or run a pack/publish dry run against the configured packageRoot.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package smoke test or release harness check that builds @eddacraft/anvil-docs-meta, packs the configured publish root with npm/pnpm dry-run, and asserts each package.json main/types/export target exists within that root.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/docs-meta/package.json and/or packages/docs-meta/project.json, plus a packaging smoke test if release tooling has a local harness.

items.title: Metadata tables are accepted even when they are not immediately after the H1
items.recommendation: Replace the broad table scan with an adjacency check over the top-level nodes immediately following the H1. The parser should require the next two relevant siblings to be the metadata and relationship tables and throw ParseError when non-table content appears before them.
items.reproduction:
Parse Markdown shaped as '# Title

Intro text before metadata.

| Type | Authority | Owner | Status | Freshness | ...' followed by the relationship table. The current scanner skips the paragraph and accepts the tables.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The happy-path fixture places both tables directly after the H1, and the missing-table tests cover absence of tables, but no test inserts prose or a heading between the H1 and the governance tables.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parseDocGovernance test where a paragraph appears between the H1 and metadata table, asserting ParseError with sourcePath and lineNumber context.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/docs-meta/src/parser/parse-metadata.ts and packages/docs-meta/src/parser/parse-metadata.test.ts.

items.title: Snapshot loader accepts variants whose values do not match the declared flag value type
items.recommendation: Validate loaded snapshots with the canonical feature flag schema where possible, or add explicit per-variant checks for key shape, value presence, valueType compatibility, defaultVariant membership, class/status enums, and targeting shape before returning FeatureFlagSnapshot.
items.reproduction: Build a snapshot JSON with a flag declaring valueType: 'boolean', defaultVariant: 'enabled', and variants: [{ key: 'enabled', value: 'true' }]. loadSnapshot accepts it, and resolveFlag returns value: 'true' instead of a boolean.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: snapshot.test.ts covers missing flag fields, invalid valueType, and empty variants indirectly only for the latter two paths; it does not include a malformed variant object or a mismatched variant value for a declared valueType.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a loadSnapshot test that rejects a boolean flag whose variant value is a string, plus tests for missing variant.key and defaultVariant not present in variants.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/feature-flags/snapshot.ts validation and snapshot loader tests

items.title: Documented nested ports subpaths are not exported correctly
items.recommendation: Add explicit exports for ./contracts/ports and each documented port subpath, or rename emitted files to match the public subpath names. Include both types and import targets.
items.reproduction: After building the package, try importing @eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/contracts/ports or @eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/contracts/ports/kindling from outside the package; Node package exports resolution targets non-existent dist files.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests import source files by relative paths and do not exercise the package export map after build.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level build smoke test that imports the public subpaths @eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/contracts/ports, /contracts/ports/kindling, /contracts/ports/ember, and /contracts/ports/edda from the built package.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/package.json export map plus a package export smoke test

items.title: Provenance expansion can emit entries with an undefined session id
items.recommendation: Require session_ids to be non-empty in ProvenanceSummarySchema and defensively parse/validate the expanded chain before returning it, or make expandProvenanceSummary throw a clear error when observation ids cannot be associated with sessions.
items.reproduction: Create a ProvenanceSummary with one valid observation_id, session_ids: [], and valid timestamps, then call expandProvenanceSummary(summary); the first kindling_sources entry has session_id undefined.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The provenance schema tests cover empty observation_ids but do not cover empty session_ids, and the type-mapping tests only exercise expansion with at least one session id.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests asserting ProvenanceSummarySchema rejects session_ids: [] and expandProvenanceSummary cannot return a chain with missing session_id values.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/provenance.ts plus a focused regression test in provenance.test.ts or type-mappings.test.ts

items.title: Exported PACKAGE_VERSION does not match the package manifest
items.recommendation: Update PACKAGE_VERSION to match package.json, or remove the hard-coded constant and generate/read it from the manifest during the build process.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included test checks consistency between the package manifest and the exported package metadata constants.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package metadata test that reads packages/edda-stack/package.json and asserts PACKAGE_NAME and PACKAGE_VERSION match the exported constants.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/index.ts plus a small metadata consistency test

items.title: Docs-site package documentation has stale commands and framework version
items.recommendation: Update README.md to use the repository package manager commands and update AGENTS.md to match the Docusaurus version declared in package.json.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is documentation drift; the feature metadata lists no linked documentation validation tests.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/docs-site/README.md and apps/docs-site/AGENTS.md.

items.title: Docs access can be enabled without an authenticated subject
items.recommendation: Fail closed when sessionSubject is missing before evaluating the flag, or require sessionSubject in DocsEvaluationInput for any enabled result. Only attach accountTier to the evaluation context after the authenticated subject has been validated.
items.reproduction: Call evaluateDocsAccess({ accountTier: 'beta', sessionSubject: null }). The constructed context uses targetingKey 'anon-visitor' and audience.accountTier 'beta', which satisfies the enabled targeting rule.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and the included files do not contain a regression test for missing-subject access decisions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs-site feature flag test asserting that beta/pro/enterprise accountTier values return disabled when sessionSubject is null or omitted, and enabled only when both subject and eligible tier are present.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/docs-site/lib/feature-flags.ts and add a focused unit test for evaluateDocsAccess.

items.title: Bundle redirects can downgrade HTTPS and leak auth headers
items.recommendation: Validate every redirect target with the same HTTPS/localhost policy, reject cross-origin redirects by default or drop auth headers when origin changes, and add a redirect depth limit.
items.reproduction: Configure a bundle URL on HTTPS that returns 302 Location: http://attacker.example/bundle.tar.gz with bearer auth configured. downloadBundle follows the HTTP redirect with the Authorization header and treats the response as the bundle.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing redirect test only exercises an HTTP localhost redirect, which is explicitly allowed for development. It does not cover an HTTPS production URL redirecting to HTTP or to a different origin with auth configured.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BundleManager test where an HTTPS test server redirects to a non-localhost HTTP URL and assert downloadBundle fails without sending configured Authorization to the redirected origin.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleManager.downloadFile redirect handling and redirect-specific tests.

items.title: Signed bundle verification ignores unsigned extra files
items.recommendation: Enumerate bundle files, exclude only the signature manifest and explicitly allowed metadata, require the signed file set to match the bundle file set, and reject empty file lists.
items.reproduction: Create a bundle directory with signed policy.rego listed in .signatures.json, then add extra.rego that is not listed in the manifest. verifyBundle returns verified=true as long as policy.rego and the signature block are valid.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover valid listed files and tampering of a listed file, but they never add an unlisted file to a signed bundle and assert verification fails.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that signs only policy.rego, writes extra.rego into the same bundle, and expects verifyBundle to return verified=false with an unsigned-file error.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleVerifier.verifySignatureBlock plus tests for unsigned extra files and empty signature file lists.

items.title: BundleManager signature verification cannot succeed from a normal download
items.recommendation: Either add an explicit signature URL/headers flow and download the sidecar before verification, or remove this private sidecar verifier and verify extracted OPA .signatures.json through BundleVerifier.
items.reproduction: Add a bundle with a valid URL and signature_key while leaving verifySignatures at its default. downloadBundle downloads the tarball, logs Signature file not found for the temp .sig path, and returns success=false with Signature verification failed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: BundleManager tests disable signature verification globally and only assert checksum behaviour. Signature verification is tested in BundleVerifier, not through BundleManager's download path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BundleManager test with signature_key enabled and a mocked signature source, asserting a valid signed bundle succeeds and a missing signature fails with a clear configuration error.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleConfig API, BundleManager.downloadBundle signature path, and BundleManager signature tests.

items.title: ANVIL_OPA_PATH accepts an incompatible OPA version
items.recommendation: Check the verifyVersion result in the env override branch and throw a descriptive error when the binary version does not match the configured major/minor expectation.
items.reproduction: Set ANVIL_OPA_PATH to an executable script or binary that prints Version: 0.50.0 while the manager expects 1.16.1. ensureBinary returns that path instead of rejecting it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The ANVIL_OPA_PATH test only proves the path existence check happens before file-not-found errors. It does not assert that a wrong-version executable is rejected.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an ANVIL_OPA_PATH test whose mock executable prints Version: 0.50.0 and expect ensureBinary to reject with a version mismatch error.
items.minimumFixScope: OPABinaryManager.ensureBinary env override branch and one unit test.

items.title: Advertised Ed25519 bundle signatures are not verifiable with Node crypto this way
items.recommendation: Implement Ed25519 with crypto.verify(null, Buffer.from(data), publicKey, signature), or remove Ed25519 from the supported/default algorithm list until it is tested and working.
items.reproduction: Generate an Ed25519 key pair, sign the canonical files JSON with crypto.sign(null, data, privateKey), and verify a manifest with algorithm Ed25519. verifyBundle fails with a signature verification error instead of returning verified=true.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The bundle verifier tests cover RS256 and ES256 signatures, but there is no Ed25519 positive-path test despite Ed25519 being in the default allowed algorithms.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a valid Ed25519 signed bundle test using generateKeyPairSync('ed25519') and crypto.sign/verify with null digest.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleVerifier.verifySignature Ed25519 branch and one positive/negative Ed25519 test.

items.title: Failed replacement downloads delete the last cached bundle
items.recommendation: Extract replacements into a staging directory, verify checksum/signature/extraction there, then atomically swap the staging directory into place only after the replacement is complete. Preserve the old cache entry on refresh failure.
items.reproduction: Download a valid bundle with a short refresh interval, wait for expiry, then have the server return a 200 response containing invalid gzip bytes. downloadBundle returns failure after deleting the old bundle directory; getBundle then returns null.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The checksum failure test fails before the old bundle directory is removed, and there is no test for an expired cached bundle followed by an extraction failure.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that first caches a valid bundle, expires it, serves a corrupt tar.gz on refresh, and asserts downloadBundle fails while getBundle still returns the original cached path.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleManager.downloadBundle extraction/swap order and refresh-failure tests.

items.title: Structured debug data bypasses secret redaction
items.recommendation: Sanitise structured data before logging, for example by recursively walking plain objects/arrays and redacting string leaves and sensitive key names, or by serialising with a redacting replacer before console.debug. Keep Error handling explicit so stack traces remain useful but redacted.
items.reproduction: Set ANVIL_DEBUG=1 and call createDebugger('kindling')('request', { authorization: 'Bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz', token: 'ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz123456' }); the object is logged without passing through sanitizeForLog.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the implementation has no evidence of coverage for structured data redaction.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a vitest case that enables debug logging, spies on console.debug, logs an object containing bearer and GitHub-style tokens, and asserts no raw secret substrings appear in any logged argument.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/kindling-integration/src/utils/debug.ts plus focused tests for object and array data passed to createDebugger.

items.title: Task IDs are used as path segments without containment checks
items.recommendation: Validate task IDs before path construction using the APS work item ID pattern, or resolve the final path and assert it remains inside the intended locks/executions directory. Apply the same guard to read, write, delete, acquire, and release helpers.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: All tests use simple IDs such as TEST-001, TASK-001, and NONEXISTENT-001. There is no test for IDs containing path separators or traversal segments.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that call getExecutionPlanPath/deleteExecutionPlan and acquireLockFile/releaseLockFile with task IDs containing ../ or path separators, expecting validation failure and no filesystem changes outside the intended .anvil subdirectory.
items.minimumFixScope: Task ID validation or path containment checks in packages/aps/src/state/index.ts, with focused state helper tests.

items.title: Concurrent locks for different tasks can overwrite each other in state.json
items.recommendation: Serialise all state.json read-modify-write updates with a separate state-file lock, or implement compare-and-retry/merge-on-write so concurrent updates preserve unrelated task records. Keep the per-task lock for first-lock-wins semantics, but do not rely on it to protect the shared state file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The concurrency test covers multiple lockers racing for the same task only; the lock-file tests show different task lock files can be acquired independently, but there is no TaskLocker test that concurrently locks two different task IDs and asserts both records remain in state.json.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a TaskLocker test that starts concurrent locks for TEST-001 and TEST-002, then asserts both operations succeed, both state records are present, and getStatus reports both as locked. Run it repeatedly or with an injected barrier around readStateFile/writeStateFile to make the race deterministic.
items.minimumFixScope: State update path in packages/aps/src/state/index.ts plus a regression test in packages/aps/src/state/state.test.ts.

items.title: Eval silently drops all but the first Rego query expression/result
items.recommendation: Either narrow the API contract by validating/rejecting multi-result, multi-expression, or binding queries, or change EvalResult to expose the full query result shape needed by downstream callers.
items.reproduction: Evaluate a query such as `x = [1, 2, 3][_]` or `1 + 2; 3 + 4`; the facade can only return the first expression from the first result and cannot represent the remaining rows/expressions/bindings.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests cover construction, a single scalar rule, and undefined versus explicit null only; none exercise multi-expression queries, binding queries, or queries that produce more than one result row.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests for `1 + 2; 3 + 4` and `x = [1, 2, 3][_]`, asserting either a clear error for unsupported query shapes or preservation of every result/expression/binding.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `Engine::eval` result handling and tests in `crates/anvil-policy-engine/src/lib.rs`.

items.title: Bare core imports are rewritten before split logic can route symbols
items.recommendation: Handle bare @eddacraft/anvil-core imports in one path only. Either run split handling before generic path rewriting and skip the generic rewrite for bare core imports, or make processImportDeclaration ignore bare core named imports that require symbol routing.
items.reproduction: Run the transform on `import { APSPlanSchema, GateRunner, OPAExecutor } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core';`. Non-dry-run rewrites it to import all three symbols from @eddacraft/anvil-contracts instead of splitting by package.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No codemod tests are included for mixed bare imports, and the example in the function comment is not executable coverage.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a transform test asserting that a bare @eddacraft/anvil-core import containing contract, runtime, and policy symbols is rewritten into separate imports for @eddacraft/anvil-contracts, @eddacraft/anvil-runtime, and @eddacraft/anvil-policy, with dry-run reporting the same intended changes without the extra whole-import rewrite.
items.minimumFixScope: tools/codemods/src/transforms/rewrite-imports.ts

items.title: Archived imports are silently ignored despite the mapping contract requiring manual review
items.recommendation: Distinguish archived/manual-review imports from ordinary no-op imports. Return a structured result from getRewrittenPath or add an isArchivedCorePath helper, then record an error or warning in TransformResult and make the CLI summary visible, ideally with a non-zero exit code when unresolved archived imports are found.
items.reproduction: Run the import codemod on a file containing `import { detectDrift } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core/drift';`. getRewrittenPath returns undefined, processImportDeclaration returns null, and no warning or error is recorded.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no tests asserting archived subpaths are surfaced as manual-review failures.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test for an archived subpath such as @eddacraft/anvil-core/drift that expects TransformResult.errors, or a dedicated manual-review result, instead of an empty no-op result.
items.minimumFixScope: tools/codemods/src/import-mappings.ts and tools/codemods/src/transforms/rewrite-imports.ts

items.title: Split imports drop aliases and type-only semantics
items.recommendation: Carry the full named import structure through grouping, including alias and type-only information. When inserting declarations, set `isTypeOnly: importDecl.isTypeOnly()` and use ts-morph structures that preserve aliases.
items.reproduction: Run the transform on `import type { APSPlan as Plan, GateRunner as Runner } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core';` with local references to Plan and Runner. The rewritten imports will not preserve the aliases or `import type`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests cover aliased named imports or type-only split imports.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add transform tests for aliased and `import type` bare core imports that require splitting, then assert the emitted code preserves local alias names and type-only declarations.
items.minimumFixScope: tools/codemods/src/transforms/rewrite-imports.ts

items.title: Freshness guard ignores the Rust scanner and embedded registry inputs
items.recommendation: Expand the freshness check to include all local Rust inputs that affect the produced binding, at minimum Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock plus local path dependencies such as crates/anvil-checks and the embedded compiled registry, or make the package test rebuild the binding before running the Node tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing Node tests validate the behaviour of whatever binary is loaded; they do not simulate a changed upstream Rust crate or registry with an older .node binary, so the guard's dependency coverage is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test for scripts/check-binding-fresh.mjs that creates or points at a stale .node and a newer scanner/registry input outside crates/anvil-checks-napi/src, then asserts the guard exits non-zero.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-checks-napi/scripts/check-binding-fresh.mjs and, if needed, the package test script in crates/anvil-checks-napi/package.json

items.title: Nx test target bypasses the package's Node-API contract tests
items.recommendation: Add an Nx target that runs the package script, or change the existing project test target to include both the Rust test executor and `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-checks-native test` in the project's tested surface. Ensure CI invokes that target for this package.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests exist, but the project metadata shown here does not connect them to the Nx `test` target; this is an orchestration gap rather than a missing assertion inside the test files.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Run the project-level test target in CI with a deliberately missing .node binding and assert the package pretest fails; that would prove the Node package test path is actually part of the project target.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-checks-napi/project.json

items.title: Expired active proposals leak into non-expired queries and active stats
items.recommendation: Apply the same effective-active predicate consistently: for non-expired query paths, exclude rows whose expires_at <= now unless include_expired is true; for active stats use status='active' AND expires_at > now; for expiring-soon stats use expires_at > now AND expires_at <= threshold. Alternatively run processExpiredProposals transactionally before these reads, but the read predicates should still be robust.
items.reproduction: Create a proposal with ttl_days=1, advance the clock by two days without calling processExpiredProposals(), then call queryProposals({include_expired:false}) or getSummaryStats(); the proposal is still returned/counted active even though getActiveProposals would exclude it by expires_at.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included decay stats test advances time and explicitly calls processExpired before reading stats, so it never exercises stale active rows whose TTL has elapsed but status has not been updated. The included candidate-service query test uses a mocked store and only checks delegation/unchanged response.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a ProposalStore/EmberQueryApi test that creates a short-TTL proposal, advances fake time past expires_at without running processExpiredProposals(), and asserts include_expired:false queries and active summary counts exclude it while include_expired:true can still return it.
items.minimumFixScope: ProposalStore.queryProposals, ProposalStore.getStats, and EmberQueryApi.getSummaryStats expiry predicates.

items.title: Proposal confidence can be updated outside the 0..1 contract
items.recommendation: Clamp or validate confidence on update before persistence. The store should enforce the invariant as the storage boundary, and CandidateService can also normalise input to match createProposal behaviour.
items.reproduction: Create a valid proposal, call CandidateService.updateProposal(id, { confidence: 5 }), then fetch it or call getStats(); the stored proposal now has confidence 5 and averages can exceed 1.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included updateProposal test only updates summary and asserts delegation. There is no test for updating confidence, especially out-of-range confidence values.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that updates confidence with values above 1 and below 0 through CandidateService and/or ProposalStore, then asserts the returned and persisted confidence is clamped to 1 and 0 respectively, or that invalid values are rejected consistently.
items.minimumFixScope: CandidateService.updateProposal and ProposalStore.updateProposal confidence handling, plus focused tests for confidence update bounds.

items.title: README usage example imports symbols the package does not export
items.recommendation: Update the README usage snippet to import `BetaInvite` and `OtpCode`, or add compatibility exports for the documented `*Email` names if that is the intended public API.
items.reproduction: Copy the README import into a TypeScript consumer: `BetaInviteEmail` and `OtpCodeEmail` are not exported by `@eddacraft/transactional`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The render test imports the actual exported component names from relative source files and does not verify the README snippet or public package import surface.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level API smoke test that imports the documented names from `@eddacraft/transactional` and renders one template, or add a documentation snippet check if README examples are tested elsewhere.
items.minimumFixScope: README usage snippet, or `packages/transactional/emails/index.ts` if preserving the documented names is required.

items.title: Public install endpoint can be used as an unauthenticated token-verification oracle
items.recommendation: Add rate limiting or abuse protection at this route or middleware layer, and consider returning a less useful oracle response pattern if token secrecy depends on low guessability. Keep backend-side throttling as the primary control, but do not rely on it exclusively from this public proxy.
items.reproduction: POST repeated candidate accessKey values to /api/early-access/install and observe 200 with command versus 401 invalid_key while each request triggers a backend /api/v1/auth/verify call.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this feature, and there is no evidence of route-level abuse or repeated-attempt behaviour being exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add route tests that simulate repeated invalid accessKey submissions from the same client identity and assert the route eventually returns 429 or another throttled response without continuing to call the verifier.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/website/app/api/early-access/install/route.ts plus any shared middleware or rate-limit helper needed by the website app.

items.title: CommonJS dependency-cruiser config is emitted as .js inside ESM packages
items.recommendation: Emit a CommonJS extension such as dependency-cruiser.cjs, or generate ESM syntax when the nearest package.json has type: module. Keep getDCConfigPath, compiler output, and docs/tests aligned with the chosen format.
items.reproduction: Run compileArchitecture with packages/anvil/core as the workspace root, then ask Node or dependency-cruiser to load packages/anvil/core/.anvil/dependency-cruiser.js; it is a .js file under a type: module package but contains CommonJS exports.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests create temporary workspaces without a package.json type: module and only assert file existence/content, so module-format loading is never exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a compiler or dc-generator test that creates a temp workspace with package.json { "type": "module" }, writes the generated config, and verifies it can be loaded by the same mechanism dependency-cruiser will use.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/dc-generator.ts, compiler expectations, and related tests.

items.title: Layer matching ignores repeated layer directories after the source root
items.recommendation: Track the actual matched segment occurrence for each pattern, preferably choosing occurrences after the source root and closest to the file. Avoid findIndex for directory names that may appear multiple times in a path.
items.reproduction: LayerDetector.detectLayer('packages/api/src/services/api/user.ts') can select application from services rather than presentation from the closer src/services/api segment because the api match is classified using the package-name occurrence.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The monorepo tests cover package names that match layer patterns when a different after-src layer exists, but they do not cover the same layer segment appearing both before and after src.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a monorepo test for packages/api/src/services/api/user.ts, or a similar repeated segment case, asserting the closer after-src api directory wins over services.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/layer-detector.ts and packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/layer-detector.test.ts.

items.title: inferBaseline save:false still writes and can overwrite the baseline
items.recommendation: Separate baseline construction from persistence. For inferBaseline, call a pure createBaseline helper when save:false, and only call BaselineManager.save/create when saving is requested. Update the current test to assert no file is written for save:false.
items.reproduction: Call inferBaseline(workspaceRoot, { save: false }) in a workspace with an existing .anvil/architecture.json; the baseline is still written before the save flag is checked.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test asserts the current faulty behaviour instead of the documented option semantics, so the regression suite would preserve the overwrite.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Change the save:false test to prewrite a sentinel baseline, call inferBaseline with save:false, and assert the sentinel file content remains unchanged.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/analyzer.ts, packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/analyzer.test.ts, and possibly BaselineManager API naming if a pure constructor helper is needed.

items.title: Generated no-orphans rule matches normal dependencies
items.recommendation: Generate the orphan rule with dependency-cruiser's orphan selector, for example from: { orphan: true, pathNot: [...] }, and extend the local DCRule type so this shape is type-checked.
items.reproduction: Generate a config with detect_orphans enabled and run dependency-cruiser on a project where src/a.ts imports src/b.ts; the no-orphans rule can match that real dependency because it lacks from.orphan: true.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests only assert that a no-orphans rule exists and that its severity follows default_severity; they never parse the generated rule shape for an orphan predicate or execute dependency-cruiser against a non-orphan import graph.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a dc-generator test that parses generateDCConfig output and asserts the no-orphans rule contains from.orphan === true, plus an integration-style fixture with a normal importing module that should not be flagged as orphan.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/dc-generator.ts and its tests.

items.title: countOccurrences treats string patterns as regular expressions
items.recommendation: For string patterns, count literal occurrences without constructing a RegExp, or escape the string before regex construction. For RegExp inputs, preserve existing flags while ensuring g is present.
items.reproduction: countOccurrences('a.b', '.') returns 3 instead of 1, and countOccurrences('C++ C++', 'C++') throws a SyntaxError because C++ is parsed as a regex.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included registry test imports createDetection from utils.ts but does not exercise countOccurrences or regex/string edge cases.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add utils tests for literal string patterns containing '.', '+', '[', and for RegExp patterns with flags such as /a/i.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/base/utils.ts countOccurrences plus focused utility tests.

items.title: Adapter testing helpers silently skip expected assertions when details are absent
items.recommendation: Treat expectedPlan as requiring result.data and make assertParseFailure throw when expectedErrorCode is provided but errors are missing or empty.
items.reproduction: assertParseFailure({ success: false }, 'INVALID') returns without throwing, and testParse can return a parse result with expectedPlan set but no data without checking the expected plan fields.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included registry tests do not import or exercise AdapterTester, testParse, or assertParseFailure.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add testing utility tests proving expectedPlan without data fails and expectedErrorCode without errors fails.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/base/testing.ts assertion branches plus focused tests for the helper utilities.

items.title: Exact planning-file confidence bonus is never applied to discovered paths
items.recommendation: Use basename(filename) for exact file-name comparisons while retaining the full path for directory-based confidence checks, or pass both path and basename explicitly.
items.reproduction: A discovered file at /repo/plan.md is scored only by substring and markdown checks, not by the exact-match branch intended for plan.md.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test file only covers AdapterRegistry behavior; there are no included tests for file discovery scoring or best-file ordering.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add file-discovery tests asserting that plan.md/prd.md discovered under a directory includes the exact-match reason and outranks weaker pattern matches.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/base/file-discovery.ts confidence calculation and a focused file-discovery test.

items.title: Baseline regeneration can erase surfaces after a validator crash
items.recommendation: Load the existing baseline before regeneration, preserve a surface's prior entry when the surface fails to produce valid JSON, and exit non-zero unless every baselineable surface produced valid JSON. Prefer writing through a temporary file only after all required surfaces have succeeded or been explicitly preserved.
items.reproduction: On a writable checkout with one surface unable to emit JSON, run `node scripts/docs/docs-check.mjs --update-baseline`; the orchestrator logs the per-surface JSON problem but still writes `docs/governance/docs-check.baseline.json` without that surface.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no linked tests, and the shown orchestrator logic has no assertion around update-baseline failure semantics or preservation of an existing baseline surface.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create a docs-check test fixture where one baselineable surface is forced to return invalid JSON, then assert `--update-baseline` exits non-zero and leaves that surface's previous baseline entry intact.
items.minimumFixScope: `scripts/docs/docs-check.mjs` regeneration logic plus one focused shell contract test.

items.title: Root package version is behind the documented release tag
items.recommendation: Either bump the root package version to 0.7.0-beta as part of the release closeout, or remove/private-scope the package-version-to-release-tag check so private root metadata is not treated as product release truth.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise README, package metadata, and drift-check release-record consistency together; the drift check only observes the mismatch when a release record is passed.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a release-readiness fixture for the current release tag that asserts package.json, README release status, changelog, and release-record expectations are internally consistent.
items.minimumFixScope: Root package metadata or the release drift-check contract, depending on which file is meant to be authoritative.

items.title: Root docs-check scripts import undeclared runtime packages
items.recommendation: Declare the root-executed validator dependencies in the root package.json, at minimum globby and any remark/unified packages those scripts import directly, then refresh the lockfile.
items.reproduction: Run `node scripts/docs/check-links.mjs --json` from the repository root in the inspected install; Node fails with `Cannot find package 'globby' imported from .../scripts/docs/check-links.mjs`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are listed for this feature, and the package-level docs-check contract tests cannot protect a clean install if the direct module import fails before test assertions run.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs-check contract case that runs each surface script directly with `--json` in a clean pnpm install and asserts the process reaches JSON output rather than failing during ESM resolution.
items.minimumFixScope: Root package.json dependency metadata and lockfile only.

items.title: Package exports do not expose the ports index subpath
items.recommendation: Add an exact package export for ./contracts/ports pointing at ./dist/contracts/ports/index.js and ./dist/contracts/ports/index.d.ts, or change the build/source layout so the wildcard target actually emits dist/contracts/ports.js.
items.reproduction: Build the package, then import '@eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/contracts/ports' from a package consumer. Node/package export resolution will look for ./dist/contracts/ports.js rather than ./dist/contracts/ports/index.js.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for package export resolution, and type-only internal imports through relative paths or the top-level contracts barrel do not exercise the published subpath.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package export smoke test that builds @eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack and imports/types imports '@eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/contracts/ports' from outside the package boundary.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/package.json exports map plus a package-boundary import smoke test.

items.title: Proposal resolution contract permits promoted proposals without a memory link
items.recommendation: Make ResolveProposalInput a discriminated union: promoted requires memory_id, dismissed/expired must not require it. Consider requiring resolution_reason for dismissal if that is part of the intended audit contract.
items.reproduction: A caller can compile code equivalent to resolveProposal(id, { status: 'promoted', resolved_by: 'agent' }) because memory_id is optional even for promoted status.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied for the ports contracts. Existing API shape tests would not fail because the current type explicitly accepts the invalid promoted-without-memory-id shape.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a type-level test using expectTypeOf or ts-expect-error showing that { status: 'promoted' } without memory_id is rejected while promoted with memory_id and dismissed/expired without memory_id remain accepted.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/ports/ember.port.ts ResolveProposalInput type and any callers that construct promoted resolution inputs.

items.title: Freshness guard ignores native build inputs outside src
items.recommendation: Include Cargo.toml and any other native build inputs that affect the N-API artefact in the freshness comparison, or compute the newest mtime across an explicit allowlist such as src/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock when relevant, and build.rs if present.
items.reproduction: Build the binding, then touch or edit crates/anvil-checks-napi/Cargo.toml without changing src/. Running the pretest script will still pass because srcMtime remains older than the .node file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are provided for this script, and package.json only wires it as a pretest hook. There is no evidence of a fixture that mutates non-src native build inputs and asserts the guard fails.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Node test that creates a temporary package layout with src/ older than a fake .node file but Cargo.toml newer, then asserts the freshness check exits non-zero.
items.minimumFixScope: Update crates/anvil-checks-napi/scripts/check-binding-fresh.mjs to include non-src native build inputs in the newest-source timestamp calculation, plus a focused regression test if the script is made testable.

items.title: QueryStatus serializes to an undocumented command name instead of the documented JSON-RPC method
items.recommendation: Do not expose QueryStatus through the serializable command-envelope enum unless the daemon accepts that wire shape. Either remove/split the variant from the serde wire enum, add a custom serde implementation that rejects command-envelope QueryStatus, or add an explicit supported route and tests for the `query-status` command form.
items.reproduction: Construct `IpcEnvelope::request("req", IpcCommand::QueryStatus)` and serialize it with serde_json; it produces a command-envelope frame containing `"command":"query-status"`, not a JSON-RPC frame with `"method":"query_status"`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test module covers list-sessions, unblock-cascade, unblock-worktree, and unknown commands, but has no test that serializes or deserializes IpcCommand::QueryStatus or checks it against the documented `query_status` JSON-RPC method contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a proto test asserting that QueryStatus cannot be serialized as a command-envelope frame, or, if command-envelope support is intended, add a round-trip test that pins `{"command":"query-status"}` and pair it with daemon routing coverage for that exact frame.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the QueryStatus representation in `crates/anvil-intercept-proto/src/lib.rs` and add a focused serialization/deserialization test for the chosen contract.

items.title: Empty authorship attestations cannot round-trip through the serializer
items.recommendation: Either reject empty attestations at createAuthorshipLog/schema boundaries or update parseAuthorshipLog to handle a separator at offset 0. The choice should match whether metadata-only authorship notes are valid for this API.
items.reproduction: Call serializeAuthorshipLog with { attestations: {}, metadata: validMetadata } and then call parseAuthorshipLog on the result; parsing throws 'missing --- separator'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: serializer.test.ts only round-trips sampleLog with two attested files; there is no empty-attestation or empty fileLineMap case.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a serializer round-trip test for an AuthorshipLog with empty attestations, or add a createAuthorshipLog test that rejects an empty fileLineMap if empty notes are invalid.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/provenance/git-ai-standard/serializer.ts and, depending on intended contract, packages/anvil/core/src/provenance/collector.ts/types.ts.

items.title: Concurrent provenance saves can drop index entries and statistics
items.recommendation: Guard index updates with an inter-process lock, or use an append-only/index-rebuild strategy that merges existing on-disk records before writing. At minimum, reload and merge the current index immediately before the final rename under a lock.
items.reproduction: Start two separate Node processes that construct ProvenanceStore for the same workspace and call save() at the same time against an existing index; after both complete, inspect .anvil/history/index.json and observe that only one of the two new records may be indexed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: provenance.test.ts saves records sequentially in one process, so there is no inter-process race around loadIndex/saveIndex.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a concurrency test that saves multiple records to the same temp workspace from worker processes and asserts index.records and statistics include every saved record.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/provenance/store.ts index update path.

items.title: Corrupt authorship notes are silently hidden or partially accepted
items.recommendation: Make parseAttestationSection throw on any non-empty malformed attestation line, and make readAuthorshipNote return null only for the specific git-notes 'no note found' failure. Re-throw parse and validation errors so callers can repair or report corrupt provenance.
items.reproduction: Create a git note under refs/notes/ai with valid metadata but an attestation line such as '  not-a-hex-hash 1-10'; parseAuthorshipLog returns a log with the file entry emptied instead of rejecting it. Create a note with malformed metadata JSON; readAuthorshipNote returns null instead of reporting a corrupt note.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: serializer.test.ts checks missing separators and malformed JSON only through parseAuthorshipLog, not through readAuthorshipNote, and it has no malformed attestation-line case.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that parse a note with an invalid attestation line and expect a thrown malformed-attestation error, plus a git-notes read test that distinguishes a missing note from invalid note content.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/provenance/git-ai-standard/serializer.ts and packages/anvil/core/src/provenance/git-ai-standard/git-notes.ts error handling.

items.title: Authorship note temp files are created with default readable permissions
items.recommendation: Create the temp file with mode 0o600, preferably via open/write/close or writeFile with { encoding: 'utf-8', mode: 0o600, flag: 'wx' }, and keep the random name cleanup path.
items.reproduction: Set umask 022, call writeAuthorshipNote with prompt text in the log, and observe the temporary file is created under os.tmpdir() with default world-readable permissions before it is unlinked.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked serializer tests validate note content format only, and provenance.test.ts does not exercise writeAuthorshipNote or file permissions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a git-notes test that stubs or observes the temp file creation path and asserts the note file is created with owner-only permissions before cleanup.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/provenance/git-ai-standard/git-notes.ts writeAuthorshipNote temp-file creation.

items.title: Named-pipe EOF is surfaced as an OS error despite the documented Ok(0) contract
items.recommendation: Map the expected pipe EOF condition, at least ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE and any other documented named-pipe EOF status used by this handle mode, to Ok(0). Keep other ReadFile failures as io::Error::last_os_error().
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included client/server test writes a payload and reads it back before shutdown; it never closes the server side before the client read, so the ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE path is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Windows test that creates an owner-only pipe server, connects a client, accepts the connection, drops or shuts down the server without writing, then asserts client.read(&mut buf) returns Ok(0).
items.minimumFixScope: OwnerOnlyPipeClient::read plus a focused Windows EOF regression test.
