items.recommendation: Copy packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/templates/*.yaml into the matching dist/architecture/templates directory during build or prepack, and ensure package files includes the copied YAML assets. Keep the runtime path resolution aligned with the emitted JS location.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests import the source module from ./index.js and run in the source tree where the YAML files exist, so they validate development-time loading but not the built or packed package layout.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a packaging/build test that runs the package build, then imports dist/architecture/templates/index.js or the public architecture export from dist and verifies getTemplate('layered') succeeds without relying on src files.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the core package build or prepack pipeline to emit template YAML files into dist/architecture/templates, adjust package inclusion if needed, and add one built-artifact regression test.

items.title: Registry comparison still depends on JSON object key order
items.recommendation: Use a deterministic deep-equality comparison after deleting ignored fields, or canonicalise both objects by recursively sorting object keys before serialising.
items.reproduction: Run the compiler once, reorder keys in an object inside patterns/compiled/registry.json without changing values, then run patterns:check. The parsed registries are semantically equivalent but stringify in different orders, causing --check to fail as stale.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this script, and there is no evidence of a case that compares semantically equivalent registry JSON with reordered keys.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test for registriesMatch or a script-level check fixture where existing JSON has the same registry data as the fresh compile but with object keys in a different order; assert it is accepted.
items.minimumFixScope: Change registriesMatch to perform recursive canonicalisation or deep equality for parsed JSON values.

items.reproduction: Install the package with dev dependencies omitted, then run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/admin-cli start`; the script requires `tsx`, which is declared only under devDependencies.

items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level smoke check that builds `@eddacraft/admin-cli` and runs its `start` script or `node ./dist/index.js --help` in an environment without devDependencies.

items.title: Successful OTP verification leaves sibling active OTP codes usable
items.recommendation: On successful verification, invalidate all active OTP codes for the user in the same atomic operation as consuming the matched code, or change the request path to invalidate prior codes when issuing a new one. Keep the matched-code atomic guard so concurrent reuse of the same code still fails.
items.reproduction: Request multiple OTPs for the same active user before expiry. Verify with one code successfully. Then submit a different still-active code for the same email; the route will find the sibling code, consume it, and issue another refresh token because only the first matching row was consumed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The happy-path test only returns one active OTP row, so it verifies single-code consumption but never exercises a user with multiple active sibling codes after a successful verification.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a POST /auth/otp/verify test where findActiveOtpCodes returns the matching code plus another active code, then assert the implementation consumes or invalidates all active codes for that user and that the sibling code cannot be used in a second verification.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the OTP verify success path and its DB query helper contract to invalidate all active OTP codes for the user after a matched code is atomically accepted; add a focused route test for the multi-active-code success case.

items.title: Unauthenticated device flow can mint tokens for any active email
items.recommendation: Do not treat email plus returned device code as authentication. Require `/confirm` to run under an authenticated user session, verified OTP/email-link challenge, or equivalent proof of email ownership, and bind the confirmed code to that authenticated user rather than trusting a submitted email string. Keep `/poll` token issuance contingent on that authenticated confirmation.
items.reproduction: POST `/auth/device/start` with `{ "email": "victim@example.com" }` for any active user, save `userCode` and `pollToken`, POST `/auth/device/confirm` with `{ "email": "victim@example.com", "userCode": "<returned>" }`, then POST `/auth/device/poll` with `{ "pollToken": "<returned>" }`. The implementation will issue credentials once the mocked DB paths correspond to an active user.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover the intended happy paths for `/start`, `/confirm`, and `/poll` separately, but they do not include an adversarial end-to-end test proving that an unauthenticated caller cannot complete the whole chain for another active user's email.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an end-to-end route test that starts a device flow for an active email and then attempts to confirm it without an authenticated activation context; the confirm should fail and poll should never return a licence or refresh token. Add a positive test where confirmation succeeds only when the activation request carries the chosen auth proof for the same user.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the `/confirm` route contract and implementation, update the linked auth-device tests, and update README endpoint auth documentation if the endpoint is no longer truly unauthenticated.

items.title: Refresh rotation consumes the old token before all fallible work completes
items.recommendation: Make refresh rotation atomic from the client's perspective. Prefer wrapping consume-plus-insert in a transaction and only committing when the replacement token can be returned, or otherwise defer irreversible consumption until all later fallible work needed for the response has succeeded. Also ensure failures after insertion do not orphan an undisclosed refresh token.
items.reproduction: Configure findRefreshTokenByHash and findUserById to return valid rows, have consumeRefreshToken resolve true, then make insertRefreshToken, findActiveScopesForUser, or signLicence reject. The request fails after the original refresh token has already been consumed and no usable replacement is returned.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests cover the happy path and expected 401 branches, but all downstream calls after consume are mocked to succeed by default and no test injects a failure after consumeRefreshToken succeeds.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test where consumeRefreshToken succeeds and insertRefreshToken or signLicence rejects, then assert the implementation does not leave the original token consumed without returning a replacement, using a transaction mock or reordered call expectations appropriate to the chosen fix.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/anvil-api/src/routes/auth-session.ts to make token consumption/replacement failure-safe, with a focused regression test in apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/auth-session.test.ts.

items.title: OTP active-code limit can be exceeded by concurrent requests
items.recommendation: Make the cap enforcement atomic at the database boundary, for example by performing the count and insert in one transaction with an appropriate user-level lock, or by moving the guarded insert into a single query that only inserts when the active count is below the limit.
items.reproduction: Start with a user having 2 active OTP codes. Send two POST /auth/otp/request requests concurrently. If both countActiveOtpCodes calls return 2 before either insert completes, both requests insert a new OTP, leaving 4 active codes despite MAX_ACTIVE_CODES being 3.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included rate-limit tests only mock sequential counts and inserts. They verify behaviour when countActiveOtpCodes returns 3, but they do not simulate concurrent requests observing the same pre-insert count.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration-style test around the real query/transaction path, or a route test with deferred mocks, that fires two concurrent /auth/otp/request calls when the mocked active count starts below the limit and asserts only one insert succeeds.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/auth-otp.ts plus the OTP insert/count query layer if the atomic guard belongs in db/queries.

items.title: Failed email delivery still consumes an active OTP slot
items.recommendation: Preserve the uniform success response, but avoid counting undelivered codes as active. Options include sending before inserting, marking failed-delivery OTPs unusable/consumed, deleting the inserted row on delivery failure, or recording delivery state and excluding failed sends from countActiveOtpCodes/findActiveOtpCodes.
items.reproduction: For an active user with no active OTPs, make sendOtpCode return { sent: false }. POST /auth/otp/request returns 200 but insertOtpCode has already run. Repeat three times within 10 minutes; subsequent requests hit the active-code cap and no email is attempted.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The provider-failure test asserts only status/body. It does not assert whether an OTP row remains active after sendOtpCode reports failure or whether subsequent requests become rate-limited by undelivered codes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend the email-provider-failure case to assert the route either does not leave an active OTP row behind or marks it excluded from future active-code counts, while still returning the same success response.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/auth-otp.ts and possibly the OTP schema/query helpers if delivery state or cleanup is implemented below the route.

items.title: Global rate limiting can mask the health check result

items.reproduction: Send more than the configured global limit of GET /api/v1/health requests within one limiter window from the same x-forwarded-for value; the limiter will return 429 before the health handler executes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests import `index.ts` for CORS preflight coverage, but none send GET `/api/v1/health` or exercise its interaction with the global middleware stack.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an `index` or `health` test that performs enough GET `/api/v1/health` requests to exceed the normal global limiter and asserts the route still returns the health contract rather than 429.

items.recommendation: Keep waitlist approval state stable across email changes. The smallest safe fix is to update or merge the matching waitlist row in the same transaction, or add an explicit immutable approval link/status instead of deriving approval only by current email equality.
items.reproduction: Have a waitlist row and beta_users row for old@example.com, call POST /admin/user/email-update with new@example.com, then list pending waitlist entries or batch approve. The old@example.com waitlist row satisfies bu.id IS NULL and is treated as unapproved.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The email-update tests cover the route response, normalization, direct beta_users collisions, and deletion races, but they do not exercise waitlist listing or batch approval after an email change.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test or query-level fixture where a waitlist row and beta user start with the same email, POST /admin/user/email-update changes the beta user email, and subsequent pending waitlist/batch approval logic does not select the old address.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/admin.ts plus the waitlist approval/listing query contract in apps/anvil-api/src/db/queries.ts, with focused admin tests.

items.title: A failed race update still writes a successful email-change audit row
items.recommendation: Make the audit insert conditional on the update result, for example with a CTE that inserts audit rows only from the updated row, or split the flow so no audit insert is issued when UPDATE ... RETURNING is empty.
items.reproduction: Delete the beta_users row after findUserByEmail succeeds but before the transaction executes. The transaction can return an empty update result and a populated audit result, then the handler returns 404 while the audit row remains committed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing deletion-race test asserts the 404 response but explicitly mocks a transaction result that includes an audit row, so it does not fail on the false audit side effect.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a deletion-race test that verifies no user.email.updated audit statement is committed when UPDATE beta_users returns zero rows, ideally against a fake transaction executor or SQL shape that can prove the audit insert is conditional.

items.title: Explicit-any test would pass duplicate or spurious AP-003 detections

items.title: Empty-catch detection lacks a non-empty catch negative test

items.title: Absent-shape driver compatibility is documented but not exercised

Reusing the payload from `validate_write_response_omits_protection_claim_when_daemon_unreachable` or constructing a minimal absent-shape payload would cover the documented contract.

items.title: Optional runner env file is omitted from the gitignore hygiene check when absent

items.title: Synthetic external smoke does not exercise positive SURFENV-001 detection

items.title: Template drift test can pass vacuously when no drift findings are emitted

items.title: Timeout regression is only tested on the successful handshake path
items.recommendation: Add a negative timeout integration test using an installed MCP entry whose command hangs or never emits a JSON-RPC initialize response, then assert `status --verify` returns within the expected budget plus tight CI slack and does not promote the client.

items.title: Runtime exclude test does not exercise a violation-producing change
items.recommendation: Make the runtime write use a fixture that would emit a violation when unfiltered, or add a paired control in the same test/suite showing the same runtime change emits a violation without `exclude_patterns`. Then assert that only the excluded configuration suppresses it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test only asserts absence of vendor violation events after writing a benign file, so it does not prove the exclude predicate was applied to a violation-producing runtime event.

items.title: Test counts clean JSON lines but does not verify every writer's record survived
items.recommendation: Collect parsed WitnessLine values and assert that the observed seq or commit_sha set exactly matches the expected values for all thread IDs.

items.minimumFixScope: Extend the existing parse loop in run_concurrent to retain parsed lines and assert expected unique writer IDs.

items.title: Concurrency test does not force simultaneous append contention
items.recommendation: Add an Arc<Barrier> shared by all worker threads and the main thread, have workers wait before calling append, then release them together after all handles are spawned.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Both test cases call the same run_concurrent helper, so neither variant guarantees overlapping append attempts.

items.minimumFixScope: Update run_concurrent in crates/anvil-witness/tests/concurrency.rs to synchronise thread start before append.

items.title: Bare-exclude JSON stream test can pass without any stdout event
items.recommendation: After parsing, assert that the captured envelopes contain `WatchEventType::Snapshot`, or assert that `lines` includes the matching snapshot before checking stderr routing.

items.title: Windows build excludes every positive violation assertion

items.title: Auth-failure test depends on host networking state
items.recommendation: Avoid a magic external port. Bind a local TcpListener to port 0 for a deterministic test double, or use an explicitly invalid/unroutable endpoint only if the CLI contract maps that exact failure mode to authentication_required across platforms.

items.title: Fixture update mode is racy under the default Rust test harness
items.recommendation: Make update mode single-owner and deterministic: either combine generation and verification into one test, skip round-trip verification while updating, use a serial test guard, or document and enforce `-- --test-threads=1` for fixture regeneration. Prefer atomic write-to-temp-then-rename if tests can ever read while updating.

items.title: Claimed resolution-chain coverage is absent from the integration entrypoint

items.title: `--check --insecure-skip-verify` tests are not exercising the intended update verification behaviour

Avoid using the real `update --check` network/update probe as a parser surrogate.

items.title: Audit hard-codes current SURFENV rules, so new rules can bypass it

items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests only use valid examples and assert selected scalar fields; they do not check the type-to-payload relationship as a cross-type invariant.

items.minimumFixScope: Add event pairing assertions or a small test helper in crates/anvil-kernel-types/tests/type_invariants.rs.

items.title: `start --json` test accepts forbidden and wrong states
items.recommendation: Strengthen `start_json_emits_state_literal_in_status_verify_shape` to assert the concrete expected read-only fresh result, at minimum `state == "needs_action"` or the intended fresh JSON state, and explicitly reject `protecting`. Also assert the complete status-verify JSON key set if the contract is that the shape matches `anvil status --verify --json`.
items.reproduction: Change the JSON renderer or start command to emit `{"state":"protecting","headline":"x","config":"absent"}` for this path; this test would still pass despite violating the stated fresh-repo guardrail.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included JSON test is the intended coverage, but it only checks enum membership and three field types. The stronger human-output tests do not parse the JSON surface, so a JSON-only regression can pass.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update `start_json_emits_state_literal_in_status_verify_shape` to assert exact state and all required LAUNCH-012 keys for a fresh temp repo/home, mirroring the status JSON contract test.
items.minimumFixScope: One integration test assertion update in `crates/anvil-cli/tests/start.rs`.

items.title: Production wire-up test never proves registered tagged writes still pass
items.recommendation: Add a run_foreground integration case that registers a session over the same daemon socket with a lineage anchor for the test process and a matching AgentTag, then sends scan_buffer with the encoded same tag and asserts there is no spoof_block and no spoof fence recorded.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tagged test intentionally registers no session before scanning, and the second test omits env_agent_tag entirely, so neither proves the production listener uses the same populated registry for register-session and scan_buffer cross-checks.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Start the daemon, compute pid_starttime(std::process::id()), send session.register with agent_tag and lineage for that PID, then send scan_buffer with env_agent_tag set to the encoded same tag. Assert result.spoof_block is absent/null and the fence store does not contain degraded:spoofed-attribution.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend crates/anvil-intercept/tests/spoof_cross_check_wired.rs with one positive registered-lineage integration test and any small helper needed to send session.register with lineage.

items.title: Claimed status, confidence, and since filters are not exercised
items.recommendation: Add integration tests with mixed memory entries that invoke --status, --confidence, and --since explicitly and assert both total and returned IDs.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing default-status test only covers the implicit active default, not explicit --status parsing, and no test command passes --confidence or --since.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create memories with varied statuses, confidence levels, and created_at values, then run `anvil --no-tui edda list --json --status superseded`, `--confidence high`, and `--since <timestamp>` and assert excluded IDs are absent.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend crates/anvil-cli/tests/edda_list.rs with explicit filter cases for the missing flags.

items.title: JSON mode does not prove full memory files are loaded
items.recommendation: Make at least one JSON test distinguish index-only metadata from full-memory data, then assert a field only present or only correct in the full memory file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current assertions rely on fields already present in index.yaml and never assert full-memory-only fields such as context, provenance, attribution, or evolution.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Write an index entry with a placeholder statement or omit a full-memory-only field from the index, write the correct full memory file, run `edda list --json`, and assert the JSON item includes the full memory data loaded from the path.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust one existing JSON integration test fixture and assertions, or add a dedicated JSON-loads-full-memory test in crates/anvil-cli/tests/edda_list.rs.

items.title: Dual-run harness never executes the TypeScript engine
items.recommendation: Wire run_dual to execute the real TS engine, or rename/scope the test as a scaffold until parity execution exists. Once integrated, remove the placeholder assertion and assert on known matching and intentionally divergent fixtures.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests codify the placeholder as expected behaviour and only verify Rust-only discrepancy reporting when the TS side is empty.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fixture that both Rust and TS engines should evaluate identically, run both engines through run_dual, and assert matches is true with no discrepancies.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace the hard-coded empty ts_violations assignment in run_dual with a real TS-engine invocation and update the placeholder-specific test expectations.

items.title: Workspace-root containment is only integration-tested for read-only tools
items.recommendation: Add stdio integration tests for anvil_suppress and anvil_fix where the server is started in one tempdir, workspaceRoot points at a sibling tempdir, and the response is an error while the sibling file remains unchanged. Apply the same containment pattern to any other workspaceRoot-accepting or file-mutating MCP tool as it is added.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing out-of-root tests cover anvil_status and anvil_check only; the suppress and fix tests use spawn_mcp_server_in(workspace.path()) with workspaceRoot set to that same workspace, so they only prove the allowed path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add mcp_serve_stdio_tools_call_suppress_rejects_workspace_outside_server_root and mcp_serve_stdio_tools_call_fix_rejects_workspace_outside_server_root using sibling tempdirs and unchanged-file assertions.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend crates/anvil-cli/tests/mcp_serve_stdio.rs with out-of-root negative cases for the write-capable workspaceRoot tools; if they fail, fix the corresponding MCP tool containment checks.

items.title: Lockfile hash test disables the entropy path it is meant to protect
items.recommendation: Run this case with entropy enabled, preferably with a threshold low enough to exercise the hash-like strings, and assert that no findings are returned for lockfile integrity and resolved hash lines.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This test is the only lockfile hash false-positive case in the owned file, but it disables entropy before scanning the high-entropy fixture.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Change does_not_flag_hex_hashes_in_lockfile to use config_with_entropy(...) and assert findings.is_empty() for the lockfile fixture.
items.minimumFixScope: Update crates/anvil-checks/tests/secret_detection.rs lockfile false-positive test configuration and assertion.

items.title: Air-gapped harness calls have no per-test timeout
items.recommendation: Run the harness through a bounded child process helper with a short timeout; on timeout, kill the child and fail the test with captured stdout/stderr and argv.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current clean-exit assertions are only reached after `cmd.output()` returns, so a hang prevents the assertion from executing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Introduce a tiny test-only command or harness mode that sleeps past the timeout and assert the helper kills it and reports a timeout failure.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace blocking `cmd.output()` in both air-gapped helpers with a timeout-aware spawn/wait implementation or a small shared test utility.

items.title: Status air-gap coverage can pass despite attempted network work
items.recommendation: Tighten the status assertions to prove the local probe path was used: parse the JSON output and assert the expected local diagnostic shape, assert absence of network/auth/update error markers, or extend the harness to detect socket/connect attempts and fail on any such attempt.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests deliberately accept any exit code and do not inspect the successful local status payload or count network attempts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a status fixture with expired credentials and assert `status --verify --json` returns the expected local activation diagnostic JSON while the harness reports zero socket/connect attempts.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `crates/anvil-cli/tests/air_gapped.rs` assertions and, if needed, the network-blocked harness contract to expose network-attempt detection.

items.title: Busy response assertion does not enforce JSON-RPC id echo
items.recommendation: Change the public busy assertion to take an expected id, or provide an `assert_busy_response_for(response, idx_or_id)` helper that validates `response["id"]` alongside the existing busy error shape.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The local integration test checks `contract-busy-99` separately after calling the public assertion, so the public helper's missing id check is not caught.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test that passes a busy-shaped response with the wrong id to the public busy assertion and expects it to panic.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `assert_busy_response`'s signature or add a stricter companion helper, then update local and downstream callers.

items.title: Blocking-rule tests can leave parked workers when an assertion fails
items.recommendation: Wrap the blocking sections in a guard that releases the barrier on drop, or structure the tests so cleanup runs even when assertions panic. For async tests, a small RAII guard plus explicit disarm after normal release is enough.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests pass on the current implementation, so the panic cleanup path is never exercised.
items.minimumFixScope: Add panic-safe cleanup around `timing_out_rule_service` and `saturating_rule_service` users in this test file.

items.title: Shared contract API is trapped inside an integration test target
items.recommendation: Move the reusable request builders, assertions, fixture list, and helper services into a library-visible test-support module or small dev-support crate, then have `tests/midedit_contract.rs` import and exercise that API.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests execute this file as its own integration test binary; they do not try to consume the fixture from another crate or integration-test target.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a consumer integration test in the intended downstream crate that imports the shared fixture API through the supported crate path and runs at least `run_full_contract`.
items.minimumFixScope: Expose the fixture API from a reusable crate/module and update this integration test to consume it.

items.title: Fixture regeneration mode can race with fixture readback tests
items.recommendation: Make update mode single-writer and non-racy: skip readback assertions when `ANVIL_UPDATE_FIXTURES` is set, move fixture writes into one dedicated test, use atomic temp-file-and-rename writes, or mark the relevant tests serial.
items.reproduction: Run `ANVIL_UPDATE_FIXTURES=1 cargo test --test protection_claim_cross_surface` repeatedly with default test threading while the fixture files are being rewritten.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Normal CI does not set `ANVIL_UPDATE_FIXTURES`, so the concurrent update path is not exercised by the regular test run.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Run the fixture update path under a serialisation guard and assert all expected fixture files exist and parse after the update completes.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust this test file's update-mode control flow so fixture writes complete before any readback test attempts to parse the same files.

items.title: Cross-surface parity test only validates the shared helper, not the surfaces
items.recommendation: Add at least one assertion that exercises each render surface through its actual rendering path with the same fixed `DaemonStatusV1` snapshot, then parse the emitted claim and compare it to the canonical `ProtectionClaim`. If full CLI/MCP execution is too heavy, factor the surface formatting logic behind testable functions and call those instead of relying on source-text pins.
items.reproduction: Change one render surface to call the shared helper but drop or alter the emitted `ProtectionClaim` after the call; these tests still validate only the direct helper result and source substrings.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover helper output, fixture bytes generated from helper output, and source substring presence. None of them execute `status`, `doctor`, or MCP validation output paths.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mutate one surface formatter in a test-only harness so it receives the correct helper claim but emits a different claim, and assert the cross-surface parity test fails.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend the integration test or adjacent render helpers so each claimed Rust surface is invoked and its emitted `ProtectionClaim` is compared against the shared expected claim.

items.title: Baseline suppression tests miss same-name symbol collisions
items.recommendation: Add collision fixtures with two distinct symbol IDs and different files but the same symbol name: mark the original as previously public or privileged, add the second symbol in the delta, and assert the expansion violation is still emitted for the new file/symbol identity. If the implementation fails, change baseline keys to include file and/or stable symbol identity rather than name alone.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing suppression tests contain only a single previously known symbol, and the mixed public baseline test uses `knownExport` versus `brandNewExport`, so no same-name collision path is exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add `same_name_different_file_public_symbol_still_flags_new_export` and the analogous privileged-access test in `crates/anvil-kernel/tests/architecture_parity.rs`.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend `crates/anvil-kernel/tests/architecture_parity.rs`; if the new test fails, update GraphDelta baseline identity and the public/privilege invariant suppression checks.

items.title: Duration formatting can render an invalid 60-second remainder
items.recommendation: Round the total duration first, then derive minutes and seconds from that rounded total, or avoid rounding the remainder upward to 60 without carrying into minutes.
items.reproduction: Render `MetricCard` with `value="3599.6"` and `format="duration"`; the displayed value becomes `59m 60s`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for `metric-card.tsx`, and there is no regression coverage for fractional duration inputs near minute boundaries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a component or unit test for `format="duration"` with `value="3599.6"` expecting `60m 0s` or the chosen normalised equivalent.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `formatValue` duration handling in `packages/libs/render/src/components/metric-card.tsx` and add focused coverage for duration boundary cases.

items.title: StatusBadge has no regression coverage for its public status mapping
items.recommendation: Add a small vitest React component test that renders all four supported statuses and verifies the expected label and status indicator are present.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists an empty tests array, and no linked test file was supplied as evidence for this review.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Table-test pass, fail, warn, and info render paths, asserting each status renders its label and the expected status indicator or accessible status text.
items.minimumFixScope: Add a test file for StatusBadge in the render package and include it in the existing vitest run.

items.title: Status semantics are not exposed to assistive technology
items.recommendation: Expose the status in the accessible name, for example with aria-label={`${status}: ${label}`} on the container and aria-hidden on the glyph, or render a visually hidden status text while keeping the visible layout unchanged.
items.reproduction: Render <StatusBadge status="fail" label="Build" /> and inspect the accessibility tree; there is no stable accessible status text such as "fail" unless the caller duplicates it in label.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the package test script only establishes that vitest is available; there is no evidence of accessibility assertions for StatusBadge.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a React rendering test that verifies the badge has an accessible name containing both the status and label, and that the visual glyph is hidden from assistive technology if it is decorative.
items.minimumFixScope: Update StatusBadge markup in packages/libs/render/src/components/status-badge.tsx and add a focused component test.
